data.name: Fertilizer
data.description: May be worth a few coins.
data.article: Fertilizer is a material used to help plants grow, often described as special dirt. It is needed to complete projects like Avian Alarm and is required for the Unexpected Initiative quest, where it must be delivered alongside a Water Pump. You can obtain it by scavenging from garden beds and wicker baskets. It also appears in greenhouses found in the Village on the Blue Gate map, and in hydroponic domes located on the Dam Battlegrounds map. This material can be recycled into other resources and can be sold for coins.

data.name: Film Reel
data.description: May be worth a few coins.
data.article:
A Film Reel is a collectible item that can be sold for coins.

You can find this item inside residential loot containers such as drawers and cabinets. Look for it in the Pale Apartments and Ruby Residence areas of the Dam Battlegrounds map. It also appears in Plaza Rosa and Grandioso Apartments in the Buried City map, and the Village in the Blue Gate map.

data.name: Fine Wristwatch
data.description: Perfect for telling the time, and showcasing that you're an exceedingly dignified person.
data.article: The Fine Wristwatch is a decorative item from an older time that has a base value of 3000 coins. This item can be found by scavenging containers such as lockers. It appears in the Buried City map, the Dam Battlegrounds map, the Blue Gate map, and the Stella Montis map, particularly within commercial and residential areas. It is also obtainable during the Night Raid event.

data.name: Finger Gun Single Shot (Emote)
data.description: A new cosmetic will be added to your collection
data.article: The Finger Gun Single Shot (Emote) is a way for your character to express themselves by performing a hand gesture that looks like shooting a gun. Raiders use this action for non-verbal communication and personal expression during gameplay. You can select this emote from your character's emote wheel.

data.name: Fireball Burner
data.description: Can be recycled into ARC Alloy.

guide_links.label: Destroy Ticks, Fireballs and Pops: Weekly Trials

data.article: The Fireball Burner is a throwable item that creates a small fire when it hits something. This fire damages nearby Fireballs and Raiders within its area. After it's used, you can pick up a Damaged Fireball Burner from where it landed. This item is important for upgrading your Refiner and is also required to complete the What Goes Around quest. You can also use it to craft other items or recycle it for useful resources. It is obtained by scavenging destroyed ARCs, specifically by defeating Fireballs and Couriers.

data.name: Firecracker
data.description: A device that sparks and pops in a pleasant manner.
data.article: The Firecracker is a common throwable item that creates a pleasant effect when used. Raiders can obtain this item by scavenging, crafting it at a Utility Station using collected resources, or purchasing it from the vendor Shani. If no longer needed, it can be recycled into various materials.

data.name: Firefly Burner
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.flavor_text: A volatile cansiter that vents fire when shot.
data.article: The Firefly Burner is a volatile canister that can be thrown and shot to vent fire and explode. This item is obtained by defeating Fireflies. Beyond its direct use, it is used to craft various items and is also needed to complete certain projects. It can also be recycled or salvaged to obtain crafting materials.

data.name: Fireworks Box
data.description: A remotely triggered arrangement of dazzling fireworks, sure to put on a show.
data.article: The Fireworks Box is a utility item that launches a dazzling display of fireworks when deployed and remotely triggered. You can craft this item at an Explosives Station after learning the Fireworks Box Blueprint, which is rewarded upon completing the Test Case quest or can be found during the "Cold Snap" map condition. You can also purchase it from Shani for 60 coins, with a daily limit of three. Additionally, three of these items can be obtained from Raider Deck AR/RD 002: Goalie, on Page 2.

data.name: Fireworks Box Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Fireworks Box
data.article: The Fireworks Box Blueprint is a blueprint that lets you craft a Fireworks Box. This blueprint can be found as a reward for completing certain quests. Additionally, it is often discovered in breachable containers and lockers during the Cold Snap event. Raiders have reported finding it in areas like the Water Treatment and Power Generation Complex within the Dam map, in hospital lockers on the Buried City map, and near extraction vents in the Blue Gate map. The blueprint has a value of 5000 coins.

data.name: First Wave Compass
data.description: Dusty but functional, these helped chart a course when when all seemed lost.

data.name: First Wave Rations
data.description: Often heated above discreet fires, these meager provisions are said to have fueled a resistance.

data.name: First Wave Tape
data.description: An old tape found inside a battered old camcorder.

data.name: Flame Spray
data.description: A classic makeshift weapon, sure to leave scorch marks.
data.article: The Flame Spray is an Uncommon Gadget that lets you spray fire at enemies. It is a weapon you craft during a raid, which requires a specific skill called In-Round Crafting. This item can also be obtained from certain Raider Decks, such as the 'IMPROVISATION PACK' found in Raider Deck AR/RD 001: Ryder & Voyager. To repair it, you will need salvage materials.

data.name: Flashy Duck
data.description: Lovingly hand-painted by someone of great talent—clearly. Any guesses who?
data.flavor_text: Can be thrown to create noise.
data.article: The Flashy Duck is a decorative trinket, which is a variant of the rubber duck. You can display it in your Raider Den stash for decoration or throw it during a raid to create noise and distract enemies. This item is found inside chimneys while the Bird City event is active. Other variants include the Alien Duck, Doodly Duck, Familiar Duck, Gentle Duck, and Tropical Duck.

data.name: Flow Controller
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Flow Controller is a rare item primarily used for recycling into crafting materials. It is also needed to complete the Snap And Salvage quest, which requires one Magnetron and one Flow Controller. You can find this item by scavenging in the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Flushing Terminal Key
data.description: A pungent key used to operate the Flushing Terminals in the tunnels below Spaceport.
data.article: The Flushing Terminal Key is a quest item used to progress The Stench of Corruption. Raiders use this key to activate a specific Flushing Terminal located in the underground tunnels of the Spaceport map. To obtain it, search a clothing rack in the Staff Locker Room within the Departure Building, also on the Spaceport map.

data.name: Fluted Rotor Core
data.description: Used to craft amplified weapons.

data.name: Food Wrapper
data.description: The vibrant colors and natural stickiness have made them a favorite among the more artistic Speranzans.

data.name: Fossilized Lightning
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: Fossilized Lightning is an Epic item that serves as a crafting resource. You can break it down to obtain other crafting materials. To find this item, you need to be aware of the Electromagnetic Storm map condition; it occasionally appears at the epicenter of lightning strikes during these events. This item is collected by scavenging it from the environment.

data.name: Free Loadout Augment
data.description: Basic augment for rookie Raiders, offering slightly more backpack space and carry capacity.
data.article: The Free Loadout Augment is a basic augment designed to increase a Raider's carrying capacity. It provides slightly more backpack space, allowing for a maximum of 35.0 weight, and is compatible with light shields. Raiders receive this augment at no cost when choosing to deploy with a Free Loadout. It can be exchanged with Lance for other basic augments, such as the Looting Mk. 1, Combat Mk. 1, or Tactical Mk. 1. Additionally, it can be recycled for resources or sold for coins.

data.name: Frequency Modulation Box
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Frequency Modulation Box is a rare item. It is needed for specific projects, such as Stage 4 of Expedition 2. You can also recycle it into various resources. These items are found by scavenging objects and containers within the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Fried Motherboard
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Fried Motherboard is primarily used to upgrade the Utility Station. You can also recycle it into general crafting materials. Look for Fried Motherboards by scavenging from containers such as Server Racks and Recording Panels.

data.name: Frigate Diagnostic Node
data.description: Found in the trail of ARC Frigates, the electromagnetic signatures of these nodes turn out to be partially decipherable.

data.name: Frigate Inductor
data.description: Can be used to upgrade the Research Station.

data.name: Frosty Duck
data.description: A dapper little fellow.

data.name: Fruit Mix
data.description: A food item that moderately increases both health and stamina.
data.article: The Fruit Mix is a food item that helps you recover. Eating it will increase your health by 25 and your stamina by 50. You can create this item using in-round crafting.

data.name: Frying Pan
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Frying Pan is a rare item you can find by searching through the environment, also known as scavenging. It serves a practical purpose as it can be recycled into crafting materials, helping you gather resources for other item projects. Raiders often discover Frying Pans in residential areas, particularly when the Flickering Flames Event is active.

data.name: Garlic Press
data.description: It'll press garlic, olives, and probably many other things.
data.article: The Garlic Press is primarily valued for the materials it provides. It is especially useful for recycling, where it yields salvage. Raiders can also choose to sell this item for coins, and it is known to fetch a higher value than some other common items.

data.name: Gas Grenade
data.description: A grenade that emits a lingering toxic cloud on impact, draining the stamina of any Raiders within its area of effect.
data.article: The Gas Grenade is a throwable item that creates a toxic cloud on impact. This cloud drains the stamina of any Raiders caught inside its area. It can be found through scavenging in the environment. Raiders can also craft it at an Explosives Station or purchase it from Apollo for coins. Additionally, it is used to craft other items at various stations. It can also be recycled for resources.

data.name: Gas Grenade Trap
data.description: A laser trip wire that detonates a Gas Grenade.
data.article: The Gas Grenade Trap is a device that projects a visible red laser. When something crosses this laser, it triggers a gas grenade, releasing a cloud of gas. This gas drains the stamina of anyone caught in its fumes. You can place this trap on most surfaces, but its laser is clearly visible. If it hasn't detonated, the Raider who placed it can disarm and recover it. It is crafted at Workbench.

data.name: Gas Mine
data.description: A proximity-triggered mine that pops up and deploys a gas cloud that rapidly drains stamina.
data.article: A Gas Mine is a deployable item that activates when ARCs enter its detection range. When triggered, it releases a cloud of gas that rapidly drains the stamina of Raiders caught within its radius and makes it harder for them to see. This effect lasts for a limited time, making it useful for controlling ARC movement or creating an escape route. You can craft it at an Explosives Station level 1, but you will first need to learn the Gas Mine Blueprint. Additionally, it can be bought directly from Apollo. If you have extra, they can be recycled to recover some basic resources.

data.name: Gas Mine Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Gas Mine
data.article: The Gas Mine Blueprint is a blueprint that unlocks the crafting recipe for the Gas Mine. Once you use this blueprint in Speranza, the recipe becomes permanently available, and the blueprint is consumed. With the recipe learned, you can then craft it at an Explosives Station level 1. It is a mine that is triggered when ARCs get near, releasing a cloud of gas that quickly drains their stamina and makes it difficult for them to see.

data.name: Geiger Counter
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Geiger Counter is a device you can recycle for crafting materials. It is also used in various projects. You can find this item by scavenging in the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Gentle Duck
data.description: Udderly adorable.
data.flavor_text: Can be thrown to create noise.
data.article: The Gentle Duck is a collectible item that you can place in your Hideout for decoration. It can also be thrown to create noise, which is useful for distracting ARCs. You can find this duck by scavenging inside chimneys when the Bird City event is active. As a variant of the Rubber Duck, it belongs to a collection that also includes the Alien Duck, Doodly Duck, Familiar Duck, Flashy Duck, and Tropical Duck.

data.name: Glitched ARC Circuitry
data.description: A hefty, electro-mechanical part with integrated magnetic circuitry. Perhaps used for data storage or processing.
data.flavor_text: 100 Merits upon return to Speranza.

data.name: Glitched ARC Light Ring
data.description: A circular light located on the undercarriage of the glitched Wasp.
data.flavor_text: 50 Merits upon return to Speranza.

data.name: Glitched ARC Phased Array
data.description: A part composed of hundreds of miniscule repeating metallic cells. It exhibits electrical integration and appears mechanically immobile.
data.flavor_text: 25 Merits upon return to Speranza.

data.name: Glitched ARC Power Converter
data.description: A compact, cylindrical part with multiple metallic layers. Its industrial architecture suggests a heavy-duty energy transformation function.
data.flavor_text: 10 Merits upon return to Speranza.

data.name: Glitched ARC Transmitter
data.description: A metallic part with a hollow center, like a socket or port waiting for a plug, with four antenna-like prongs at its corners.
data.flavor_text: 15 Merits upon return to Speranza.

data.name: Goggles (Radio Renegade Variant)
data.description: Radio Renegade cosmetic variant - unlocked by completing A Warm Place to Rest quest.
data.article: The Goggles (Radio Renegade Variant) are a cosmetic item used to change the appearance of your character's headgear. They are a distinctive part of the Radio Renegade outfit style, allowing Raiders to customize their look. To obtain them, you must successfully complete the A Warm Place to Rest quest.

data.name: Gothic Graffiti (Aviator Color)
data.description: A new cosmetic variant will be added to your collection.
data.article: The Gothic Graffiti (Aviator Color) is a cosmetic item that adds a new visual style to your collection, allowing you to customize your in-game appearance. Raiders can obtain this item through Twitch drops, which are special rewards provided during certain official ARC Raiders streams on Twitch.

data.name: Grappling Hook
data.description: A simple gadget that anchors to most surfaces, allowing users to navigate hard-to-reach places.

data.name: Grappling Hook Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Grappling Hook

data.name: Great Mullein
data.description: Used to craft medical supplies.
data.article: Great Mullein is a plant resource that can be collected in the game world. It is found as a natural spawn in various areas across the Buried City map. Raiders gather this item directly from the environment; it is not obtained by looting arcs or looting containers.

data.name: Green Light Stick
data.description: A throwable chemical light that illuminates the area around it.
data.flavor_text: Illumination Radius 7m
data.article: The Green Light Stick is a specific type of light stick. It is a distinct item often categorized alongside the Blue Light Stick.

data.name: Green Light Stick Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Green Light Stick.
data.article: The Green Light Stick Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft a Green Light Stick.

data.name: Hairpin I
data.description: Has a built-in silencer. Great for stealth, but tricky in combat.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Hairpin I is a pistol that uses Light Ammo. It is a common rarity weapon, notable for its built-in silencer, which makes it effective for stealth. Raiders can obtain it through scavenging, by crafting it at Workbench, or by purchasing it from Tian Wen. This item serves as a base for crafting more advanced versions, such as Hairpin II, Hairpin III, and Hairpin IV. It can also be recycled for various resources.

data.name: Hairpin II
data.description: Has a built-in silencer. Great for stealth, but tricky in combat.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Hairpin II is an upgraded pistol that uses light ammo and features a built-in silencer. This improved model offers a 10% increased fire rate, 13% reduced reload time, and increased durability. It can be crafted at a Gunsmith bench. It can also be recycled for resources or have its durability restored.

data.name: Hairpin III
data.description: Has a built-in silencer. Great for stealth, but tricky in combat.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Hairpin III is an upgraded slide-action pistol that uses light ammo and features a built-in silencer. Compared to earlier versions, it provides an increased fire rate, faster reloading, and improved durability. You can craft this pistol at the Gunsmith using various components. It can also be repaired using various materials or recycled to recover resources.

data.name: Hairpin IV
data.description: Has a built-in silencer. Great for stealth, but tricky in combat.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Hairpin IV is an upgraded slide-action Pistol that uses Light Ammo. It comes with a built-in silencer, making it suitable for stealth during encounters. Upgrading to Hairpin IV increases its fire rate, reduces its reload time, and boosts its durability compared to previous versions.

You can craft the Hairpin IV by upgrading a Hairpin III at a Gunsmith, using various other materials. It can also be recycled or salvaged to recover some resources. When sold, it fetches 2,900 coins.

data.name: Hand Drill
data.description: Used in crafting.

data.name: Happy Jig (Emote)
data.description: Maintain at least a  Rookie II rank in trials until season end.
data.article: The Happy Jig is an emote that allows your character to perform a specific dance in the game. It is a cosmetic item used for self-expression. Raiders can obtain this emote by achieving at least a Rookie II rank in trials and keeping that rank until the end of the season.

data.name: Harmonica
data.description: A playable harmonica used to attract ARC's attention, and impress other Raiders.

data.name: Headphones
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: Headphones are a rare item Raiders can find in the game. Their primary purpose is to be recycled, providing Raiders with useful crafting materials and components. Raiders typically obtain them by scavenging in residential and commercial areas.

data.name: Heavy Ammo
data.description: Heavy bullets used mainly with large-caliber weapons.
data.article:
Heavy Ammo is a type of ammunition for high-caliber weapons. It helps you take down ARCs more effectively because it can penetrate their armor better than Medium Ammo and Light Ammo, though it is not as strong as Launcher Ammo.

You can find Heavy Ammo by scavenging, or it might drop from defeated ARCs such as the Rocketeer, Rocketeer Husk, and Sentinel. It can also be found in Raider Caches or purchased from the vendor Tian Wen. You can craft it at a Workbench.

data.name: Heavy Fuze Grenade
data.description: A grenade that detonates after a delay, dealing explosive damage in its radius.
data.article: The Heavy Fuze Grenade is an explosive device that detonates after a short delay, creating a large blast that damages ARCs in its area. Raiders can find this grenade by scavenging in the environment or craft it at an Explosives Station level 3.

data.name: Heavy Gun Parts
data.description: Used to craft weapons.
data.article: Heavy Gun Parts are a material used to upgrade, craft, and repair weapons. Raiders can find them by searching in Security and Raider areas, or by salvaging them from defeated Bombardiers and Rocketeers. Additionally, they can be crafted at a Refiner after learning a blueprint. They can also be purchased from Celeste.

data.name: Heavy Gun Parts Blueprint
data.description: Used directly in crafting items of all tiers.
data.article: The Heavy Gun Parts Blueprint is a schematic that teaches you how to craft Heavy Gun Parts at a Refiner. This process requires crafting materials as ingredients. They are then used to upgrade, craft, and repair various weapons, and are also a component in creating other items at a Gunsmith.

data.name: Heavy Shield
data.description: A heavy shield that blocks a large portion of incoming damage, but carries a significant cost to mobility.
data.article: The Heavy Shield is an equipable item that blocks a large portion of incoming damage, though it reduces your character's movement speed. To use this shield, Raiders must have specific augmentations equipped, including Combat Mk. 2, Combat Mk. 3 (Aggressive), Looting Mk. 3 (Safekeeper), or Tactical Mk. 3 (Defensive). It can be crafted at a Gear Bench, found through scavenging, or purchased from Lance with coins. This item can be repaired with resources or recycled into other materials.

data.name: Helmet (Radio Renegade Variant)
data.description: Radio Renegade Helmet Variant - Unlocks by completing Flickering Threat Quest
data.article: The Helmet (Radio Renegade Variant) is a cosmetic item that Raiders can equip to customize the appearance of their character. This specific helmet style is part of the Radio Renegade outfit.

data.name: Herbal Bandage
data.description: An improvised medical item that gradually restores health over time.
data.article: The Herbal Bandage is an improvised medical item that slowly restores your health over time. When used, it heals you for 3.5 health per second over 10 seconds. You can craft this item at a Medical Lab using salvage materials. Alternatively, it can be crafted if you have the Traveling Tinkerer skill. It can also be obtained from certain in-game decks.

data.name: Hidden Bunker Key
data.description: A makeshift key that lets you open a bunker in Spaceport

data.name: High-Voltage Exposure
data.description: Some ARC machines appear capable of absorbing energy before putting it back to use. The same principle might be worth testing on something a little less insulated.

data.name: Horizontal Grip
data.description: Moderately reduces both vertical recoil and horizontal recoil.
data.flavor_text: 30% Reduced Horizontal Recoil - 30% Reduced ADS Speed
data.article: The Horizontal Grip is a weapon modification that helps improve stability when firing. When attached to a compatible weapon, it reduces both vertical recoil and horizontal recoil by 30%. This grip also causes a 30% reduction in the speed at which Raiders can aim down sights. This modification can be broken down into various components and resources through recycling.

data.name: Hornet Driver
data.description: Can be recycled into ARC Alloy.
data.article:
The Hornet Driver is a thrown item that temporarily stuns nearby Hornets for seven seconds and other Raiders for half a second within a six-meter range. It is obtained by scavenging destroyed Hornets. Once thrown, a Damaged Hornet Driver can be retrieved from where it landed.

This item is used to craft tools. It is also required to upgrade the Gear Bench and progress through the The Trifecta quest. Additionally, it contributes to the Trophy Display project.

data.name: Household Cleaner
data.description: Can be recycled into chemicals.
data.article: The Household Cleaner is an uncommon item that serves as a valuable source of crafting materials. You can recycle this item to break it down into various resources, which are important for your crafting and upgrade efforts. To obtain it, search containers and explore residential areas.

data.name: Hullcracker Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft an Hullcracker
data.article: The Hullcracker Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Hullcracker I at the Gunsmith. You can obtain this blueprint as a reward upon completing the quest called "The Major's Footlocker". For an overview of available tasks, visit the Quests page.

data.name: Hullcracker I
data.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
data.article:
The Hullcracker I is a pump-action Grenade Launcher that fires explosive projectiles. These projectiles only detonate when they hit an ARC, making it effective for targeting enemy armor. It uses launcher ammo.

You can craft Hullcracker I at a Gunsmith bench level 1 once you have learned the Hullcracker Blueprint. It can also be found through scavenging or bought from the vendor Tian Wen for coins.

Hullcracker I can be used as a base to craft upgraded versions, such as Hullcracker II, Hullcracker III, and Hullcracker IV. It can also be recycled for resources or salvaged for materials.

data.name: Hullcracker II
data.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
data.article:
Hullcracker II is an upgraded version of the Hullcracker I, a special pump-action Grenade Launcher. This weapon fires explosive projectiles that only detonate upon hitting an ARC, making it effective for breaking through enemy defenses. It offers an 18% increased fire rate and +10 durability compared to its predecessor.

You can craft this weapon at a Gunsmith bench using a Hullcracker I and other crafting materials. The blueprint for the initial Hullcracker is rewarded from the quest The Major's Footlocker.

It can be further upgraded at a Gunsmith bench into more powerful versions, or recycled for materials.

data.name: Hullcracker III
data.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
data.article:
The Hullcracker III is an upgraded version of the Hullcracker, a special pump-action launcher that uses launcher ammo. It fires explosive projectiles designed to detonate only when hitting ARCs. Its strong armor penetration helps reveal ARC weak spots.

This specific model has a higher fire rate and increased durability compared to earlier versions.

Raiders craft the Hullcracker III by upgrading the Hullcracker II at the Gunsmith.

data.name: Hullcracker IV
data.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
data.article:
The Hullcracker IV is an upgraded pump-action grenade launcher that fires special explosive projectiles. These projectiles are designed to only detonate when they hit an ARC, making the weapon effective for breaking through their defenses. It uses launcher ammo.

This weapon is obtained by crafting a Hullcracker III at a Gunsmith crafting station.

data.name: Humidifier
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: A Humidifier is a crafting material and can also be recycled into other resources. Raiders need Humidifiers to progress through certain projects, such as stage 4 of the Expedition 1 project. You can obtain Humidifiers by scavenging within the Buried City, with a guaranteed appearance in the Red Tower lockers.

data.name: Husk Lily
data.description: These beautiful, but toxic flowers only grow around Baron husks. As for why, your guess is as good as anyone's.

data.name: Ice Cream Scooper
data.description: It is theorized that scooping things was a favorite pastime in the world before.
data.article: The Ice Cream Scooper is a component that can be recycled for resources or sold for coins.

data.name: Il Toro Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft an Il Toro
data.article: The Il Toro Blueprint is a blueprint that allows Raiders to create the Il Toro shotgun at a Gunsmith bench. It is known for its high damage output at close distances.

data.name: Il Toro I
data.description: Has a large bullet spread, sharp falloff, and high damage output.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Il Toro I is a pump-action shotgun that uses Shotgun Ammo. It is effective for dealing high damage to enemies at close range.

You can find the Il Toro I by scavenging, or purchase it from Tian Wen. It can also be crafted at a Workbench or Gunsmith, facilities often found in your Hideout, once you have learned the Il Toro Blueprint and gathered the necessary materials.

This shotgun can be upgraded into the Il Toro II, Il Toro III, and Il Toro IV at a Gunsmith using crafting materials. To repair it, you will need crafting materials. You can also recycle it for general resources or salvage it for other materials. It can be sold for coins.

data.name: Il Toro II
data.description: Has a large bullet spread, sharp falloff, and high damage output.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Il Toro II is an upgraded version of the Il Toro I shotgun, designed for close-range combat. It deals high damage using ammunition. This upgraded model improves upon the base shotgun by offering an increased fire rate, a larger magazine capacity, and better durability. Raiders can craft it at a Gunsmith Bench level 1. It can also be recycled to recover useful components.

data.name: Il Toro III
data.description: Has a large bullet spread, sharp falloff, and high damage output.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: Il Toro III is an upgraded version of the Il Toro II shotgun, designed for close-range combat. Raiders can craft it at a Gunsmith by upgrading an Il Toro II with salvage materials. Compared to previous versions, it features a 35% increased fire rate, adds two rounds to its magazine capacity, and improves its durability by 20 shots. It can be further upgraded to Il Toro IV or recycled for salvage.

data.name: Il Toro IV
data.description: Has a large bullet spread, sharp falloff, and high damage output.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Il Toro IV is an advanced version of the Il Toro shotgun, designed for close-range combat. It is built upon the Il Toro III, providing a significantly increased fire rate, a larger magazine, and enhanced durability. This pump-action weapon uses ammunition and is effective for defeating enemies at close distances.

To obtain the Il Toro IV, you must upgrade an existing Il Toro III at a Gunsmith. The base Il Toro I can be crafted at a Workbench once you have learned the Il Toro Blueprint, or sometimes purchased from Tian Wen. You may also find Il Toro shotguns by scavenging in various areas. It can be repaired with materials to restore its durability.

data.name: Impure ARC Coolant
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: Impure ARC Coolant is a less refined form of ARC Coolant that serves as a general resource for crafting. Its primary purpose is to be recycled into crafting materials. Raiders obtain this item by scavenging ARC husks.

data.name: Industrial Battery
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Industrial Battery is a rare item used to upgrade the Gear Bench. It can also be recycled for materials. You can find this item by scavenging in the Dam Battlegrounds map. Specifically, look in the Hydroponic Dome Complex, within the Power Generation Complex on shelves or carts, and in car hoods.

data.name: Industrial Charger
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Industrial Charger is a rare item. It serves as an ingredient for various projects, helping you complete different requirements. You can also recycle this item to gain useful crafting materials and components. To keep track of items required for your projects, you might find the Needed Items Tracker helpful.

data.name: Industrial Magnet
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Industrial Magnet is a rare item used to craft various items and obtain materials through recycling.

data.name: Insulation Roll
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

data.name: Integrated Binoculars
data.description: Can be equipped and used like regular binoculars, but cannot be dropped or removed from their slot.

data.name: Integrated Defibrillator
data.description: Reusable Defibrillator on a fixed cooldown. Can be used like a normal Defibrillator, but cannot be dropped or removed from its slot.

data.name: Integrated Shield Recharger
data.description: Reusable Shield Recharger on a fixed cooldown. Can be used like a normal Shield Recharger, but cannot be dropped or removed from its slot.

data.name: Ion Sputter
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Ion Sputter is a resource item used in various crafting projects and can be recycled to gain crafting materials. It is required for a specific stage of the Expedition 2 project. This item is also needed for the With A View quest. You can find Ion Sputters by scavenging in the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Jolt Mine
data.description: A proximity-triggered mine that pops up and stuns anything within its radius.
data.article:
The Jolt Mine is a throwable device that helps you control ARC movement. It activates when an ARC gets close, stunning ARCs for 7 seconds and other Raiders for 4 seconds within a 5-meter area after a short delay.

You can craft it at an Explosives Station once you have learned the Jolt Mine Blueprint. It can also be purchased from Apollo for 2,550 coins, with a limit of 3 per day.

data.name: Jolt Mine Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Jolt Mine
data.article: The Jolt Mine Blueprint is a blueprint that, when used, unlocks the ability to craft the Jolt Mine. Once you learn it in Speranza, the blueprint is consumed. You can find this blueprint by scavenging from Industrial Containers across any map, or it can be obtained as a reward for completing Weekly Trials. Blueprints you have already learned are marked and cannot be used again. If you have extra blueprints, they can be sold for 5,000 coins.

data.name: Junior (Outfit)
data.description: This is the Junior cosmetic outfit
data.article: The Junior Outfit is a cosmetic item that changes the appearance of your Raider. This outfit has different versions and can also include a backpack. Raiders obtain it by playing three raids in The Finals.

data.name: Jupiter
data.description: Fires projectiles at an incredible velocity, capable of damaging multiple targets with one shot.
data.flavor_text: Very effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Jupiter is a bolt-action sniper rifle that deals a lot of damage with each shot and uses ammunition. This weapon can penetrate ARC armor, which helps in damaging larger ARCs and hitting their weak points. Raiders need to time their shots carefully due to a slight delay before firing.

You can craft the Jupiter at a Gunsmith station once you have learned the Jupiter Blueprint. It can also be found inside a Harvester. When it needs repairs, it costs certain resources. You can also recycle it to obtain salvage materials.

data.name: Jupiter Blueprint
data.description: Fires projectiles at an incredible velocity, capable of damaging multiple targets with one shot.
data.article: The Jupiter Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Jupiter at a Gunsmith bench. Raiders obtain this blueprint by solving the Harvester puzzle protected by the Queen during the Harvester minor map condition.

data.name: Kettle I
data.description: Quick and accurate, but has low bullet velocity and takes a long time to reload.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Kettle I is a semi-automatic assault rifle that fires ammunition. This weapon is used for combat.

You can obtain the Kettle I by crafting it at the Gunsmith. It is also available for purchase from Tian Wen. Additionally, Raiders might receive it as part of a Free Loadout kit. It can be recycled for materials.

data.name: Kettle II
data.description: Quick and accurate, but has low bullet velocity and takes a long time to reload.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Kettle II is an upgraded semi-automatic assault rifle that uses light ammo. It improves upon the Kettle I by offering faster bullet velocity and reduced reload time, along with increased durability, making it more effective in combat. Raiders can craft it at a Gunsmith by upgrading a Kettle I with additional components.

data.name: Kettle III
data.description: Quick and accurate, but has low bullet velocity and takes a long time to reload.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Kettle III is an upgraded semi-automatic assault rifle that uses light ammo. This version of the Kettle offers improved bullet velocity, faster reloading, and increased durability compared to earlier models, making it a more effective weapon for combat. You can craft it at Gunsmith. Once obtained, it can be repaired using materials to restore its durability, recycled to recover resources, or sold for coins.

data.name: Kettle IV
data.description: Quick and accurate, but has low bullet velocity and takes a long time to reload.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article: Kettle IV is the most refined version of the Kettle semi-automatic assault rifle. It is designed for accuracy and quick firing, using light ammo. This upgraded version offers a significant increase in bullet velocity, a faster reload speed, and improved durability compared to previous Kettle models. Raiders craft it at a Gunsmith by upgrading a Kettle III using crafting materials. It can also be recycled for resources or sold for coins.

data.name: Kinetic Converter
data.description: Moderately increases fire rate.
data.flavor_text: 20% Increased Horizontal Recoil
data.article: The Kinetic Converter is a weapon modification designed to alter how your weapon functions. Its primary effect is to increase your weapon's rate of fire. When attached, it will also cause your weapon to experience increased horizontal and vertical recoil during use. This modification can be recycled to recover various resources and other materials.

data.name: Laboratory Reagents
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: Laboratory Reagents are a crafting material used to upgrade the Explosives Station. These reagents can be found by scavenging in medical areas. They can also be recycled into general crafting materials.

data.name: Lance's Mixtape (5th edition)
data.description: Lance has personally planted a number of these around the Rust Belt, for some reason.
data.article: Lance's Mixtape (5th Edition) can be sold for coins.

data.name: Laser Level
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

data.name: Laser Trap: Lure
data.description: A deployable laser trip wire that detonates a Lure Grenade.
data.article: The Laser Trap: Lure is a blueprint that teaches you how to create a special trap. It sets up a laser tripwire that stretches up to 5 meters. When anything crosses this laser, the trap activates and releases a lure, which helps draw nearby ARCs towards its location. The trap can only be disarmed and picked up by the Raider who placed it, unless another Raider has the Minesweeper skill.

data.name: Launcher Ammo
data.description: Anti-ARC payloads used mainly by the Hullcracker.
data.flavor_text: Compatible with Hullcracker
data.article:
Launcher Ammo is a type of ammunition used by specific weapons, such as the Hullcracker and the Rascal. It features an explosive payload designed to effectively penetrate ARC armor, providing a stronger option than Heavy Ammo.

  • It can be scavenged from the environment.
  • It is obtained by looting arcs like the Turbine and Bombardier.
  • Raiders can craft it at the Workbench using salvage materials.
  • It is also available for purchase from Tian Wen.

data.name: Leaper Pulse Unit
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
The Leaper Pulse Unit is a throwable device that creates a temporary damaging singularity, affecting both ARCs and Raiders within its area. After being used, a damaged unit can be retrieved.

You obtain this item by salvaging defeated Leapers. It is also needed for upgrading the Utility Station and completing the Into The Fray quest. It can also be recycled for resources.

data.name: Lemon
data.description: Can be consumed for a small amount of stamina.
data.article: Lemon is a resource in the game. It is often mentioned alongside apricot in discussions and guides that highlight specific locations where these items can be found.

data.name: “Leviathan's Crown” Ship Model
data.description: A majestic sight in any era, this fierce merchant ship is indifferent to the aerodynamic benefits of fiberglass technology.
data.article: The "Leviathan's Crown" Ship Model is a unique trinket primarily used for decoration. Its main purpose is to allow Raiders to personalize their Raider Den by displaying it within their stash and it also sells for a pretty penny.

data.name: Library Book
data.description: A literary masterpiece filled with fantastical worlds, callously earmarked by some uncultured oaf.

data.name: LiDAR Scanner
data.description: A laser-based scanner used to detect the subtlest changes to the Earth's surface
data.article: A Lidar Scanner is a specialized device used to monitor ground tremors and gather data. Its primary purpose is to help complete the Eyes In The Sky quest. During this quest, you install it at high points, such as the Communications Tower in the Spaceport, to get a clear signal.

data.name: Light Ammo
data.description: Light bullets used mainly with SMGs and light handguns. Such as Kettle, Stitcher, Burletta, Hairpin and Bobcat.
data.article: Light Ammo is a type of ammunition used by low-caliber weapons. This ammo type is not very good at going through ARC armor. You can obtain Light Ammo in several ways: by finding it through scavenging, by opening a Raider Cache, or by looting arcs like the Turret or Wasp. It can also be crafted at a Workbench from general resources or bought from Tian Wen.

data.name: Light Bulb
data.description: Without light, life underground would be impossible.
data.article:
The Light Bulb is an uncommon trinket item. It is a necessary component for completing various projects, such as Expedition 1 and Expedition 2.

You can find these by scavenging in the Electrical Substation area of the Dam Battlegrounds map, frequently appearing inside cars and car hoods. They are also present in car hoods near the Extraction Lift in the Generator Hall area of the Dam Battlegrounds map. Additionally, look for them within loot containers and industrial loot containers at Pilgrim's Peak in The Blue Gate map.

data.name: Light Gun Parts
data.description: Assorted spare parts used for pistols and SMGs.
data.article: Light Gun Parts are assorted spare parts used for pistols and SMGs. They are used to upgrade, craft, and repair weapons that use Light Ammo. You can craft this item at the Refiner after learning the Light Gun Parts Blueprint. Additionally, Celeste sells this item in limited quantities for coins each day. This item can also be recycled into other resources.

data.name: Light Gun Parts Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft Light Gun Parts

data.name: Light Impact Grenade
data.description: A grenade that detonates on impact, dealing explosive damage in a small radius.
data.article: The Light Impact Grenade is a throwable item that explodes on contact, damaging anything nearby in a small area. While it may not deal as much damage as other explosives, it is inexpensive to create. Raiders can craft it at an Explosives Station level 1 or Workbench, or even during a raid if they have the In-Round Crafting skill. It can also be purchased from Apollo or recycled for resources.

data.name: Light Shield
data.description: A lightweight shield that blocks a small portion of incoming damage without impacting mobility.
data.article: The Light Shield is a lightweight piece of defensive gear that provides protection from incoming damage without impacting your mobility. You can find this shield through scavenging, craft it at a Workbench and a Gear Bench, or purchase it from Lance. Its durability can be restored through repairs.

data.name: Lightweight Stock
data.description: Moderately improves ADS & draw speed.
data.article: The Lightweight Stock is a weapon mod that helps you aim down sights and equip or unequip your weapon faster. To get one, you first need to acquire the Lightweight Stock blueprint. Once you have the blueprint, you can craft it at a Gunsmith. If you no longer need it, you can recycle it for salvage or coins.

data.name: Lightweight Stock Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Lightweight Stock
data.article: The Lightweight Stock Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Lightweight Stock. This weapon modification helps improve the speed at which you aim down sights and ready your weapon. You can craft it at the Gunsmith Bench level 3 using a combination of different materials.

data.name: Li'l Smoke Grenade
data.description: A grenade that pops a thick but small smoke cloud on impact, blocking visibility from ARC and other Raiders.
data.article: The Li'l Smoke Grenade is a throwable item that creates a small, thick smoke cloud when it explodes. This smoke blocks visibility for ARCs and other Raiders within a 2.5-meter radius for 6 seconds, helping you avoid detection or move unseen. You can craft this item at a Utility Station, or during a raid if you have the appropriate Inventory Skill. It can also be recycled into basic resources.

data.name: Looting Mk. 1
data.description: Basic looting augment. More backpack slots and weight capacity, but low defensive and tactical capability.
data.article:
The Looting Mk. 1 is an augment that increases the number of items you can carry in your backpack and raises your total weight capacity. It is designed to work with light shields.

You can obtain this augment in a few ways: Lance offers a free exchange service where you can trade a Free Loadout Augment for it, and you can also buy it directly from Lance. Additionally, it can be crafted at a Workshop or Gear Bench.

data.name: Looting Mk. 2
data.description: Significantly increases looting potential; adds slots for trinkets.
data.flavor_text: Automatically throws off attached Ticks after 1s.
data.article: The Looting Mk. 2 is a Looting Augment that helps you gather more items during your expeditions. It significantly increases your backpack capacity and the total weight you can carry. This augment also features a unique ability to automatically remove any Ticks attached to you after a brief moment, provides two Safe Pocket slots, and has three dedicated slots for trinkets. You can only use this augment with a light shield. It is crafted at Gear Bench using salvage.

data.name: Looting Mk. 3 (Cautious)
data.description: A looting augment that swaps some carry capacity to increase survivability.
data.flavor_text: Upon Shield break, automatically administers a weak Adrenaline Shot. Has a fixed cooldown.
data.article: The Looting MK. 3 (Cautious) is an augment designed to help Raiders survive by reducing some carry capacity in favor of defensive benefits. When your shield breaks, it automatically administers a weak adrenaline shot, which then has a fixed cooldown before it can be used again. This augment includes built-in binoculars, allows for a maximum loadout weight of 70.0, and has Light shield compatibility. You can craft this augment at a Gear Bench. It can be recycled for resources or salvaged for components, and also repaired using various materials.

data.name: Looting Mk. 3 (Safekeeper)
data.description: A looting augment that trades weight and utility for increased looting potential.
data.flavor_text: A Safe Pocket that allows any item to be stored.
data.article: The Looting Mk. 3 (Safekeeper) is an augment that provides a secure pocket, allowing you to safely store any items you find. This augment allows you to Safe-pocket a weapon - something other augments do not allow. You craft this augment at a Gear Bench after obtaining its blueprint. The Looting Mk. 3 (Safekeeper) Blueprint has been found in the Reinforced Reception area.

data.name: Looting Mk. 3 (Safekeeper) Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft the Looting Mk. 3 (Safekeeper) Augment.
data.article: The Looting MK. 3 (Safekeeper) Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to create an augment at Gear Bench. This augment provides a secure pocket for storing items found during raids and specifically allows you to Safe-pocket a weapon - something other augments do not allow.

data.name: Looting Mk. 3 (Survivor)
data.description: A heavy-duty pack mule augment. Large weight capacity and large backpack space.
data.flavor_text: While downed and stationary, health regenerates up to 75% of max downed health.
data.article: The Looting MK. 3 (Survivor) is an Augment that increases your carrying capacity and backpack space. It also has a special ability: if you get downed and stay still, your health will regenerate up to 75% of your maximum downed health.

data.name: Looting Mk. 3 (Survivor) Blueprint
data.description: A heavy-duty pack mule augment. Large weight capacity and large backpack space.
data.article: The Looting Mk. 3 (Survivor) Blueprint allows you to craft the Looting Mk. 3 (Survivor) augment at a Gear Bench. It increases your carry weight and backpack space, and provides a benefit where you can regenerate up to 75% of your health when you are downed and staying still.

data.name: Lure Grenade
data.description: A noisy device that sticks to surfaces, distracting nearby ARC machines and drawing their fire.
data.article: The Lure Grenade is a throwable item designed to create a loud noise, drawing the attention of nearby ARCs. Raiders can use this to distract ARCs and redirect their attacks, providing an opportunity to escape or reposition. Its blueprint is rewarded upon completing the Greasing Her Palms quest and can be crafted at a utility station.

data.name: Lure Grenade Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Lure Grenade
data.article: The Lure Grenade Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft Lure Grenades at a Utility Station. These grenades create noise to distract nearby ARCs, making them focus their attacks on the grenade instead of you. This blueprint is obtained as a reward from completing the Greasing Her Palms quest.

data.name: Lure Grenade Trap
data.description: A laser trip wire that detonates a Lure Grenade.
data.article: The Lure Grenade Trap is a device that projects a visible red laser trip wire. When the laser is broken, it detonates a grenade, creating a loud siren that draws the attention of nearby ARCs towards the trap. This helps Raiders distract ARCs away from their position or towards a chosen area. Raiders can craft this trap at a Workbench. If the trap has not detonated, the Raider who placed it can disarm and recover it.

data.name: Magazine Geometry 101
data.description: A standard magazine does its job, but it can only hold so much. Getting familiar with a drum-fed design could reveal how that extra room is put to use, and where the same idea might fit elsewhere.

data.name: Magnet
data.description: Used to craft a wide range of items. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
A Magnet is a common component used to create various items. You can find Magnets through general scavenging in the environment or purchase them from Celeste.

Raiders can also obtain Magnets by recycling salvage. Additionally, you can salvage them into crafting materials.

data.name: Magnetic Accelerator
data.description: Used to craft advanced weapons.
data.article:
The Magnetic Accelerator is a refined component used in crafting and repairing advanced weapons. It also serves as a key material for various projects.

You can obtain Magnetic Accelerator by looting arcs such as the Queen. It can also be found through scavenging in the game world.

This item is crafted at a Refiner, requiring salvage materials. Additionally, it can be recycled for other crafting materials.

data.name: Magnetron
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Magnetron serves as a crafting material. You can recycle it to obtain other resources needed for crafting. This item is also a requirement for the Snap And Salvage quest, where you'll need one Magnetron in addition to a Flow Controller. You can find it by scavenging throughout the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Major Aiva's Mementos
data.description: A closely-shut box, covered in many years worth of dust.

data.name: Major Aiva's Patch
data.description: A torn patch, found amidst rubble and ruin.

data.name: Marano Market Business Card
data.description: The scribbled writing on this business card almost obscures the logo of Marano's market.

data.name: Mask Fragment
data.description: Half a face, cast in bronze.

data.name: Mastery Medal (Backpack Charm)
data.description: Maintain Wildcard I trials rank until the season end.
data.article: The Mastery Medal (Backpack Charm) is a cosmetic item you can attach to your Raider's backpack. It hangs from the bottom and swings as your Raider moves, allowing you to customize your character's look. This charm is obtained by maintaining the Wildcard I rank in Trials until the season ends.

data.name: Matriarch Reactor
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.flavor_text: Used to Craft: Aphelion
data.article: The Matriarch Reactor is a component salvaged from defeated Matriarchs. It is used in crafting advanced weapons and can also be traded for account upgrades with Ermal - the Nomadic Envoys Trader.

data.name: Mechanical Components
data.description: Used to craft a wide range of items. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
Mechanical Components are a refined material used to craft, repair, and upgrade a variety of items, especially weapons. They are also essential for upgrading the Gunsmith.

You can obtain Mechanical Components by scavenging in the environment or by defeating specific ARCs like the Bastion, Bombardier, Leaper, and Shredder. Additionally, you can craft them at the Refiner by combining salvage materials.

data.name: Medium Ammo
data.description: Medium bullets used mainly with medium-caliber weapons. Such as Rattler, Tempest, Arpeggio, Renegade and Torrente.
data.article:
Medium Ammo is a type of ammunition used by weapons that fire medium-caliber rounds. It performs better at penetrating ARC armor than light ammo, but is not as effective as heavy ammo.

Raiders can obtain Medium Ammo by looting arcs like the Bastion and Hornet, or by scavenging it from Raider Caches. It can also be crafted at the Workbench, or purchased from Tian Wen.

data.name: Medium Gun Parts
data.description: Assorted spare parts used for rifles.
data.article: Medium Gun Parts are assorted spare parts used to upgrade, craft, and repair weapons. You can find these parts by scavenging through containers and environmental loot, or by looting Bastion and Sentinel ARCs. Additionally, they can be crafted at the Refiner once you have learned the Medium Gun Parts Blueprint, using salvage. Celeste also offers a daily limited stock of these parts. If you have surplus, they can be recycled for other resources.

data.name: Medium Gun Parts Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft Medium Gun Parts
data.article: The Medium Gun Parts Blueprint is a blueprint that allows Raiders to craft medium gun parts at the Refiner. These parts are a resource used in various crafting projects, primarily for building and upgrading weapon components.

data.name: Medium Shield
data.description: A standard shield that blocks a medium portion of incoming damage at a moderate cost to mobility.
data.article:
The Medium Shield is a standard shield that provides Raiders with a fair amount of protection by blocking incoming damage, at the cost of a small reduction to movement speed. It is a versatile defensive option for various situations.

Raiders can obtain the Medium Shield through several methods: by scavenging in the environment, from Raider Caches, or as an item from Raider Decks. It can also be purchased from Lance for 6000 coins, with a daily limit of three. Additionally, it can be crafted at a Gear Bench.

To equip this shield, Raiders must have one of the following Augments installed:

  • Combat Mk. 1

  • Tactical Mk. 1

  • Combat Mk. 2

  • Tactical Mk. 2

  • Combat Mk. 3 (Aggressive)

  • Looting Mk. 3 (Safekeeper)

  • Looting Mk. 3 (Survivor)

  • Tactical Mk. 3 (Defensive)

  • Tactical Mk. 3 (Healing)

data.name: Metal Brackets
data.description: Can be recycled into metal parts.
data.article: Metal Brackets are an uncommon component item. They can be recycled to obtain crafting materials.

data.name: Metal Parts
data.description: Used to craft a wide range of items.
data.article: Metal Parts are a common material used to craft a wide range of items. You can find them by searching containers and environmental objects like metal crates, car hoods, server racks, and seed vaults. This material can also be obtained by recycling salvage or by purchasing them from Celeste.

data.name: Microscope
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Microscope is a rare item primarily used to gain various crafting materials and coins when recycled. This item is found by searching containers across different areas, most reliably within the Stella Montis map. It appears frequently during the Night Raid event.

data.name: Mini Centrifuge
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Mini Centrifuge is designed to be recycled for crafting materials. Its main purpose is to provide resources that help with Raider progression and projects. You can find this item by scavenging the environment throughout Stella Montis. Upon recycling, it yields various crafting materials and other components.

data.name: Mini Pump
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

data.name: Mobile-Fire Grip Fittings
data.description: Fast movement is useful right up until a weapon needs to come into play. A weapon that keeps up with the pace would be useful.

data.name: Mod Components
data.description: Used to craft weapon mods. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: Mod Components are refined materials used to craft various weapon modifications. Raiders typically obtain them by crafting at the Refiner using other components, or by recycling salvage. Once acquired, they are essential for creating advanced weapon mods at the Gunsmith Bench.

data.name: Moisture Meter
data.description: Measures soil moisture levels for precise irrigation control.

data.name: Moss
data.description: Can be used to regain a small amount of health.
data.article: Moss restores a small amount of health over ten seconds when consumed. It is also used to craft medical supplies. You can obtain Moss by harvesting it from dead trees and inside Hydroponic Domes in the Dam Battlegrounds. It can also be found in Wicker Baskets or purchased from Celeste for 10 coins, with a daily limit of 5. If not needed for crafting or healing, it can be recycled into other resources.

data.name: Motor
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: A Motor is a mechanical component used for workbench upgrades. Its primary purpose is to help improve your Hideout by upgrading the Refiner. You can find Motors by scavenging from containers, often within car hoods in the Water Treatment area of the Dam Battlegrounds. Motors can also be recycled into general crafting materials.

data.name: Mountaineer's Detector
data.description: Useful for finding foreign objects hidden in the snow. As an added bonus, it works just as well on sand.

data.name: MRI Duck
data.description: Has technology gone too far?

data.name: Mushroom
data.description: Can be consumed to regain a small amount of health.
data.article:
Mushrooms are a healing item you can consume to recover a small amount of health. They are also used to train Scrappy.

You can find Mushrooms in various places across several maps. In the Dam Battlegrounds map, look for them on pipes in the Water Treatment Control area, along the sandy shores and inside irrigation planters of the Hydroponic Dome Complex, and on nearby trees in the Central Swamp Lift and Wreckage areas. In the Spaceport map, check the small hangar south of the East Container Yard, on a tree there, and inside underground tunnels in the center of the map. In the Riven Tides map, they grow on trees in the Dried Riverbed. They can also be found inside wicker baskets during the Lush Bloom minor map condition.

data.name: Music Album
data.description: Perfect for relaxing nights at home, casual get-togethers, and private air guitar concerts.
data.article: The Music Album is a collectible item related to the game's soundtrack. Raiders may find a use for these albums as they can be utilized for various projects.

data.name: Music Box
data.description: Worth a small fortune.
data.article: The Music Box is a collectible item primarily valued for its sell price. It can be safely sold for coins, serving as a reliable way to gain coins. It is similar to other collectible items like the Painted Box, Playing Cards, and Poster of Natural Wonders.

data.name: Smoke Grenade
data.description: A grenade that creates a lingering smoke cloud on impact, blocking visibility from ARC and other Raiders.
data.article:
A Smoke Grenade is a throwable item that releases a thick smoke cloud on impact. This cloud blocks the sight of ARCs and other Raiders, providing a way to escape or approach unseen. It lasts for 20 seconds and covers a 7.5-meter radius.

You can craft this item at a Workbench or Utility Station once you have learned the smoke grenade blueprint and gathered the necessary crafting materials. Apollo also sells the Smoke Grenade for 3,000 coins, with a daily limit of 6.

data.name: Smoke Grenade Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Smoke Grenade
data.article: A Smoke Grenade Blueprint allows you to craft smoke grenades at a Workbench or Utility Station, which create a cloud to block visibility from ARCs and other Raiders. It can be found by looting containers in Buried City as well as other maps during Night Raid or Cold Snap game types.

data.name: Smoke Grenade Trap
data.description: A laser trip wire that detonates a Smoke Grenade.
data.article:
A Smoke Grenade Trap is a device that projects a visible red laser up to five meters. When its laser beam is interrupted, it detonates a Smoke Grenade, releasing a thick gray smoke cloud. This smoke helps to hide Raider movements and obstructs the view of both ARCs and other Raiders.

You can place this device on almost any surface, but its laser is clearly visible to everyone. If a trap has not yet detonated, the Raider who placed it can disarm and pick it up.

This trap is crafted at the Workbench, requiring certain components and the "Traveling Tinkerer" skill.

data.name: Snap Blast Grenade
data.description: A grenade that sticks to surfaces, dealing explosive damage after a short delay.
data.article:
The Snap Blast Grenade is a magnetic grenade that sticks to surfaces before exploding after a short delay, dealing explosive damage. It is used in the Sparks Fly quest.

You can find this item in several ways:

  • By scavenging.
  • From containers such as Raider Caches, Security Lockers, and Weapon Cases.
  • By purchasing from Apollo for 2,400 coins, with a daily limit of 3.

This grenade can be crafted at an Explosives Station. It can also be recycled for resources.

data.name: Snap Hook
data.description: A gadget that allows the user to scale structures and cover large distances.
data.article: The Snap Hook is a gadget that helps you move quickly across areas by grappling to higher ground or managing descents. You can get a Snap Hook by completing the Lost In Transmission quest. It can also be crafted at a Utility Station once you have learned the Snap Hook Blueprint. Additionally, Snap Hooks are rewarded from certain Projects, such as Stage 5 of the Trophy Display. You can also find them listed in Raider Deck AR/RD 001: Ryder & Voyager and Raider Deck AR/RD 002: Goalie.

data.name: Snap Hook Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Snap Hook
data.article:
The Snap Hook Blueprint is a blueprint that teaches you how to build the Snap Hook, which allows you to move quickly across distances or reach higher spots. Once learned, you can craft it at a Utility Station.

You can find this blueprint during Electromagnetic Storm map condition on various maps, most commonly in Residential loot areas.

data.name: Snitch Scanner
data.description: Can be recycled into ARC Alloy.

guide_links.label: Damage Flying-based ARC Enemies: Weekly Trial

data.article:
The Snitch Scanner is a utility item you can throw to call in Wasps. Once thrown, it becomes damaged.

You obtain this item by defeating Snitches, which are a type of ARC enemy.

It is used to upgrade your Utility Station and is also an item needed to complete The Trifecta quest. Additionally, you can recycle it for salvage.

data.article: A Snowball is a compact, throwable item fashioned from malleable and aerodynamic snow. These piles appear on maps when the Cold Snap map modifier is active.

data.article: The Spaceport Control Tower Key is an access item that allows you to open a specific locked area. Its main purpose is to unlock the Control Tower in the Spaceport map, which Raiders often seek for its contents. It functions similarly to the Blue Gate Communication Tower Key, providing entry to an otherwise inaccessible tower.

data.name: Spaceport Trench Tower Key

data.article: The Spaceport Trench Tower Key is a specific key used to open secured trench tower buildings located within the Spaceport map. You can obtain Speaker Components in several ways:

  • Scavenged from containers or the environment.
  • Obtained by recycling or salvaging other items.
  • Purchased directly from Celeste.

data.name: Spectrometer

data.article: The Spectrometer is a rare item. Its primary use is to be recycled into crafting materials that can then be used in various projects. You can find this item by scavenging throughout the environment in the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Spectrum Analyzer

data.article: The Spectrum Analyzer is used to obtain valuable crafting materials. Its primary purpose is to be recycled into general materials that help you make other items. Raiders can find it by scavenging in the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Spotter Relay

data.article:
The Spotter Relay is used to progress the Trophy Display Project. When deployed, it functions as a trap that lures nearby ARCs. It is a key component for Stage 2 of the Trophy Display Project and is also needed for the quest Combat Recon. You can track all project needs on the Needed Items Tracker.

Obtain Spotter Relays by destroying Spotter Drones, which only spawn when a Bombardier ARC is active nearby. They are found on Spaceport and Buried City maps, but the north-west section of the Blue Gate map offers the most consistent encounters.

data.article: The Spring Cushion can be broken down into useful components. Its main purpose is to provide general crafting materials when you recycle it. You can find this item by searching containers like trash cans, which are commonly located in Residential and Commercial areas.

data.name: Stable Stock I

data.article: Stable Stock I is a weapon mod. It helps Raiders manage how much their weapon kicks back after firing and how spread out their shots are.

data.article:
The Stable Stock II is a weapon modification that helps make your weapon more stable. It allows your weapon to recover faster after you fire and reduces how much your shots spread.

To obtain this item, craft it at a Gunsmith Bench level 1 using a Stable Stock II Blueprint.

It can also be obtained as a reward for completing quests or by succeeding in trials.

data.name: Stable Stock III
data.description: Significantly improves dispersion & recoil recovery time.
data.article:
The Stable Stock III is a Weapon Mod that greatly improves how quickly your weapon becomes steady again after recoil and how fast its accuracy returns after shooting. Keep in mind that attaching this mod will slightly increase the time it takes to ready your weapon and put it away.

You can craft this mod at a Gunsmith bench, but you will need to have the Stable Stock III Blueprint first.

data.name: Stable Stock III Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Stable Stock III
data.article:
The Stable Stock III Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Stable Stock III weapon modification at a Gunsmith Bench. This modification improves weapon handling by reducing shot spread and recoil recovery time.

You can find this blueprint:

  • Inside containers like Boxes, Ammo Crates, Breachable Containers, and Lockers.
  • Across maps such as the Spaceport, Blue Gate, Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, and Riven Tides.
  • During events including Cold Snap, Electromagnetic Storm, Night Raid, Hurricane, and Locked Gate.

Recycling the blueprint yields coins.

data.article: The Stitcher I is a fully-automatic Submachine Gun that uses light ammo. Raiders might receive this weapon when choosing a Free Loadout, or they can find it by scavenging. data.article:
The Stitcher II is a fully-automatic Submachine Gun that uses light ammo. It is an improved version of the Stitcher I, offering less horizontal recoil, faster reload speed, and increased durability.

Raiders can craft the Stitcher II at a Gunsmith Bench by combining one Stitcher I with salvage materials. It can also be obtained as part of a Free Loadout or purchased from Tian Wen. The weapon sells for 2,000 coins.

It offers better weapon control with reduced horizontal recoil, faster reload times, and improved durability compared to its previous version. Raiders primarily obtain this weapon by crafting it at a Gunsmith from other components. It can be recycled for useful materials and resources.

data.article: The Succulent (Backpack Charm) is a cosmetic item used to customize your Raider's appearance. It attaches to the bottom of your backpack and swings as you move, adding a unique visual detail. To get this charm, you need to complete the The Root Of The Matter quest.

data.name: Surge Coil
data.description: A deployable device that periodically electrifies the area around itself and briefly stuns anything caught within it.
data.article: The Surge Coil is a deployable device that periodically electrifies the area around itself, briefly stunning anything caught within it. It also causes ARCs to redirect their attention towards it, much like a Lure Grenade. This item can be found by scavenging or crafted at the Explosives Station once you have learned its Surge Coil Blueprint. The blueprint can be obtained by looting arcs.

data.name: Surge Coil Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Surge Coil.
data.article:
The Surge Coil Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Surge Coil, a deployable device that electrifies the area around it. When placed, it periodically sends out an electric pulse that briefly stuns both ARCs and other Raiders who come too close. This can be useful for controlling areas, buying extra time during combat or looting, and escaping fast-moving ARCs like Shredders.

You can find the Surge Coil Blueprint by looting various containers, such as lockers, desk drawers, cupboards, and industrial crates, during the Electromagnetic Storm map condition. You must be in a map where this condition is active. Check the Event Timers to see when the Electromagnetic Storm is running on any map. It has been reported to drop in areas like the Testing Annex, Water Treatment Facility, and Hydroponic Domes within the Dam Battlegrounds, among others.

data.name: Surge Shield Recharger
data.description: A handheld kit that recharges a shield on use.
data.article: The Surge Shield Recharger is a handheld kit used to instantly restore 50 shield charge after a brief moment, which helps you stay protected during engagements. This item is crafted at a Medical Lab using other resources.

data.name: Surveyor Vault
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: A Surveyor Vault is a rare item used to improve your crafting abilities and complete certain projects. You will need it to upgrade your Medical Lab to level 3, which is a station found in your Hideout. It is also a requirement for the first stage of the Trophy Display project. You can obtain Surveyor Vaults by looting arcs such as the Surveyor or Courier. Additionally, you can recycle them to gain crafting materials or salvage them for resources.

data.name: Synthesized Fuel
data.description: Used to craft utility items and explosives. Can be recycled into chemicals.
data.article: Synthesized Fuel is a material used to craft explosives and other helpful items. You can also throw it, and if it gets shot, it will explode, causing damage in a small area. This material is also important for improving your Explosives Station level 1. You can find Synthesized Fuel by scavenging in the environment or by recycling other items. Additionally, Celeste sells a limited amount of Synthesized Fuel each day for coins. If you have extra, you can recycle it to get various resources.

data.name: Syringe
data.description: Used to craft medical supplies. Can be recycled into plastic.
data.article:
A Syringe is a sterile item used to craft medical supplies and is also required for the Doctor's Orders quest.

Raiders can find Syringes in containers such as bags and medical crates across Buried City, Dam Battlegrounds, Blue Gate, and Stella Montis. The trader Celeste also sells them in Dam Battlegrounds for coins. Alternatively, you can obtain a Syringe by recycling salvage.

When no longer needed, a Syringe can be recycled into crafting materials.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 1
data.description: Basic tactical augment. More Quick Use slots for more tactical choice, but limited survivability and slightly lower looting potential.
data.article:
The Tactical Mk. 1 is an Augment that adds more Quick Use slots, allowing you to carry more tactical items. While it offers five Quick Use slots and compatibility with a medium shield, it has fewer backpack slots and a lower maximum weight capacity.

You can get the Tactical Mk. 1 in a few ways. Lance offers it as a free exchange if you provide a Free Loadout Augment, or you can purchase it from him directly. It can also be crafted at a Gear Bench. Additionally, you might find this Augment by scavenging.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 2
data.description: Adds more backpack space and an extra utility item slot.
data.flavor_text: Upon Shield break, deploys a small smoke grenade. Has a fixed cooldown.
data.article: The Tactical Mk. 2 is a type of Augment that increases your backpack space and provides an additional slot for utility items. It also has a unique ability: if your shield breaks, it automatically deploys a small smoke grenade after a short cooldown. This augment is an improved version of the Tactical Mk. 1. You can craft it at a Gear Bench, and it can be repaired or recycled into general resources.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Defensive)
data.description: A defense-focused augment for keeping Shields topped up.
data.flavor_text: Allows Shield Rechargers to be used while running.
data.article:
The Tactical Mk.3 (Defensive) is an augment designed to help Raiders keep their shields full. Its main feature is a built-in shield recharger, which allows you to recharge your shields even while running. This augment also works with light, medium, and heavy shields, offering broad compatibility.

This augment can be crafted at Gear Bench once its blueprint has been learned. Blueprints for it can be found through scavenging. It can also be recycled into other resources or repaired.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Defensive) Blueprint
data.description: a defense-focused augment for keeping Shields topped up
data.article: The Tactical MK.3 (Defensive) Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Tactical Mk.3 (Defensive) augment at a Gear Bench. It helps keep your shields full, letting you use a Shield Recharger even while running.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Healing)
data.description: A healing-focused augment which adds extra slots for healing items.
data.flavor_text: When revived from being downed, releases a healing cloud that restores 20 health over 10 seconds. Has a 30-second cooldown.
data.article:
The Tactical Mk. 3 (Healing) is a tactical augment designed to improve a Raider's healing capabilities. It provides additional slots for carrying healing items in both your backpack and safe pockets. When you are revived after being downed, it releases a healing cloud that instantly restores 45 health to you and nearby Raiders. This ability has a 45-second cooldown.

This augment's Blueprint is found by participating in the Locked Gate event. Once you have the Blueprint, you can craft it at a Gear Bench. The augment can also be recycled to recover general resources.

data.article: The Tactical MK.3 (Healing) Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft a specialized augment designed for healing at Gear Bench. When equipped, the augment provides more capacity for healing items and, upon being revived from a downed state, creates a healing cloud that instantly restores 45 health. This effect has a 45-second cooldown. It can also be recycled for resources or salvaged for components.
