data.article:
The Rascal is a break-action grenade launcher that uses launcher ammo. It fires explosive projectiles designed to detonate only when they hit ARCs, making it useful for direct combat against ARCs.

Raiders can obtain the Rascal by crafting it at a Gunsmith Bench level 1. The Rascal Blueprint is required to craft the initial Rascal I. It can then be upgraded to more advanced versions, such as the Rascal II, Rascal III, and Rascal IV, by crafting them from the previous version. It can also be recycled for salvage.

data.name: Rascal Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Rascal
data.article:
The Rascal Blueprint is a rare blueprint in ARC Raiders, added in Patch 1.29.0. If you're wondering how to find the Rascal Blueprint in ARC Raiders - it drops from Raider Containers across all maps and requires a Gunsmith Workbench to craft.

Best Ways to Find the Rascal Blueprint:

  • Raider Containers — Weapon Cases, Raider Caches, and Ammo Crates are your best source across all maps.

  • Security Breach Lockers — Breach Lockers scattered across all maps have confirmed drops. Use Metaforge Interactive Maps to find them.

  • Key Rooms — Locked rooms with high loot density can also yield the blueprint as a general drop.

Tips to Maximize Rascal Blueprint Drops: Run Night Raid for boosted rare blueprint drop rates. Safe Pocket the blueprint the moment you find it. Go in naked with items to keep farming runs low-risk.

data.name: Rascal II
data.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
data.article: The Rascal II is an improved break-action grenade launcher. It fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARCs, and uses launcher ammo. This upgraded version provides 7% reduced reload time and an additional 10 durability. Raiders can craft it at a Gunsmith. It can also be found while exploring the Buried City map. When no longer needed, it can be recycled for resources.

data.name: Rascal III
data.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
data.article: The Rascal III is an upgraded break-action grenade launcher that fires explosive projectiles, which detonate only when hitting an ARC. This weapon provides a 13% reduced reload time and an additional 20 durability compared to its previous version. It uses launcher ammo. Craft it at the Gunsmith from a Rascal II and other required components, or recycle it for resources. It can be further upgraded into the Rascal IV.

data.name: Rascal IV
data.description: Fires explosive projectiles that only detonate when hitting ARC.
data.article: The Rascal IV is a further upgraded version of the Rascal, a special break-action grenade launcher. This weapon fires explosive projectiles that detonate only when they hit an ARC, making it suitable for direct combat. It uses Launcher Ammo and offers improved durability and a faster reload time compared to earlier versions. You can craft it at a Gunsmith by upgrading a Rascal III. The initial Rascal weapon requires a Rascal Blueprint to craft before it can be upgraded.

data.name: Rattler I
data.description: A cheap offensive option, but has to be reloaded 2 bullets at a time.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Rattler I is a fully-automatic assault rifle that uses medium ammo. It is an inexpensive weapon that provides good damage and accuracy for close to medium range encounters.

Raiders can obtain the Rattler I in a few ways:

  • It can be crafted at the Gunsmith.
  • It can be received as part of a Free Loadout.
  • It can also be found through scavenging.

It can be used to craft the Rattler II, or it can be recycled or salvaged for other resources.

data.name: Rattler II
data.description: A cheap offensive option, but has to be reloaded 2 bullets at a time.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Rattler II is an improved version of the Rattler I assault rifle, designed for Raiders seeking a more reliable combat option. It offers an increased magazine size and better durability compared to its previous version. This weapon fires medium ammo and provides good damage and accuracy for engaging ARCs at close to medium range.

You can craft the Rattler II at a Gunsmith by upgrading an existing Rattler I using salvage.

data.name: Rattler III
data.description: A cheap offensive option, but has to be reloaded 2 bullets at a time.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Rattler III is an upgraded version of the Rattler II assault rifle, using medium ammo. This fully-automatic weapon offers increased magazine capacity and improved durability, making it a reliable option for various combat situations. You can obtain it by crafting at the Gunsmith Bench. It can also be used as a component to further upgrade to a Rattler IV. Additionally, it can be recycled for various resources or salvaged for materials, or sold for coins.

data.name: Rattler IV
data.description: A cheap offensive option, but has to be reloaded 2 bullets at a time.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Rattler IV is an advanced version of the Rattler assault rifle, which uses medium ammo. This weapon provides a solid option for fighting ARCs at close to medium range. Compared to its previous versions, it offers an increased magazine size and improved durability.

You obtain the Rattler IV by upgrading a Rattler III at the Gunsmith. This crafting process requires other materials to complete. It can also be recycled for various resources and components.

data.name: Recorder
data.description: A playable recorder used to attract ARC's attention, and impress other Raiders.
data.article: The Recorder is a playable instrument that plays two different melodies. It can be used to attract the attention of ARCs. Other Raiders can join in by playing instruments like the Shaker and Acoustic Guitar. While playing, you cannot perform actions that require both hands.

data.name: Red Coral Jewelry
data.description: Valued for its fine craftsmanship, and effortless ability to make your eyes pop.
data.article: Red Coral Jewelry helps Raiders progress. It is found by opening red lockers located in the Buried City map.

data.name: Red Light Stick
data.description: A throwable chemical light that illuminates the area around it.
data.article: The Red Light Stick is a consumable item that provides light. It is designed for quick use to help Raiders illuminate dark surroundings, improving visibility during exploration or combat. Similar items include the Yellow Light Stick, Green Light Stick, and Blue Light Stick.

data.name: Red Light Stick Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Red Light Stick.
data.article: The Red Light Stick Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the red light stick at the appropriate crafting station.

data.name: Red (Radio Renegade Color)
data.description: A new cosmetic variant will be added to your collection.
data.article: The Red (Radio Renegade Color) is a cosmetic item used to apply a red color scheme. It is part of the Radio Renegade style, which can be used to customize the visual appearance of your radio or other parts of an outfit.

data.name: Reinforced Reception Security Code
data.description: Temporary security code to unlock the main gate.
data.flavor_text: Can only be used during Locked Gate
data.article:
The Reinforced Reception Security Code is a temporary security code used to unlock a main gate. It is one of four codes required to open the gate during the "Locked Gate" Blue Gate map condition.

You can find this code in lootable containers, such as bins, located within the Reinforced Reception area on the Blue Gate map. At least one code will appear per round during this condition, and sometimes more.

To use the code, head to the Gate Control Room on the Blue Gate map. Once inside, interact with one of the four terminals. Submitting a code consumes it and activates the terminal which helps to open the Locked Gate.

data.name: Remote Control
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Remote Control is a device used to activate specific functions, which can help you progress through areas or manage objectives. For example, it is used to open or close extraction points, allowing you to secure your salvaged items. You can find this item by searching various containers scattered across the Stella Montis map. If you have extra Remote Controls, they can be recycled into coins and other general crafting materials.

data.name: Remote Raider Flare
data.description: A deployable device that, when manually triggered, launches a Raider Distress Flare.
data.article: The Remote Raider Flare is a deployable item that, when activated, sends a Raider Distress Flare into the sky, which can be used to signal for help or mark a location. You can find this item by scavenging. It can also be crafted at a utility station if you have learned the Remote Raider Flare Blueprint and have the necessary components. Another way to get it is by purchasing it from Apollo for 810 coins. Finally, it can be obtained from the 'Decks: Raider Deck AR/RD 001: Ryder & Voyager' on Page 1, specifically within the 'MAYHEM PACK'. When no longer needed, it can be recycled for salvage.

data.name: Remote Raider Flare Blueprint
data.description: Allows you to craft the Remote Raider Flare.
data.article: The Remote Raider Flare Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to produce Remote Raider Flares at a Utility Station. A Remote Raider Flare is a deployable tool that, when activated, launches a distress signal into the sky.

data.name: Renegade I
data.description: Has high damage output, accuracy, and headshot damage.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Renegade I is a lever-action battle rifle that uses medium ammo. It offers high damage, accuracy, and increased headshot damage. This rifle is well-suited for medium to long-range encounters, and its accuracy is particularly good when you are crouching and stationary. For a stealthier approach, equipping a Silencer II or better attachment makes its shots quiet. Be aware that reloading the Renegade I is slower because each shell is loaded individually.

Raiders can obtain it in a few ways. It can be found through scavenging. It can also be crafted if you have Gunsmith skill level 3. Additionally, a vendor named Tian Wen sells it for 21,000 coins, with one item available for purchase each day.

data.name: Renegade II
data.description: Has high damage output, accuracy, and headshot damage.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Renegade II is an upgraded battle rifle that uses medium ammo. This version improves upon the original Renegade I by offering an increased fire rate, better durability, and faster accuracy recovery after firing. It is well-suited for fighting at medium to long distances due to its accuracy and high damage when hitting an enemy's head. To obtain it, craft this weapon by upgrading a Renegade I at the Gunsmith bench.

data.name: Renegade III
data.description: Has high damage output, accuracy, and headshot damage.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Renegade III is a lever-action battle rifle that uses medium ammo. It is an upgraded version of the Renegade battle rifle, offering better damage, accuracy, and headshot damage. With moderate ARC Armor Penetration, it is effective in combat against ARCs, particularly in medium to long-range encounters. This weapon also gains increased fire rate and durability compared to the Renegade II. Equipping it with a Silencer II or better can make it suitable for stealth play.

You obtain the Renegade III by upgrading a Renegade II at a Gunsmith bench, which is located in your Hideout. Its durability can be restored using salvage materials.

data.name: Renegade IV
data.description: Has high damage output, accuracy, and headshot damage.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Renegade IV is the highest upgraded version of the lever-action Battle Rifle. It features high damage output, good accuracy, and increased headshot damage, making it effective for medium to long-range engagements. When equipped with a Silencer II or better, it can be used for stealth. This rifle uses medium ammo.

You obtain the base Renegade I by scavenging or by purchasing it from Tian Wen. It is crafted at a Gunsmith bench by improving an earlier version. It offers increased fire rate and durability compared to its previous models.

data.name: Resin

data.article: Resin is a common healing item that helps you by restoring a small amount of health gradually over time, specifically 1 health per second for 10 seconds after use. You can find Resin by scavenging or by looking inside wicker baskets. Currently, its only known general use is to provide coins during the Lush Blooms and Cold Snap map conditions.

Raiders can find this item by scavenging various containers, such as Breachable Containers, standard Containers, and Lockers, located in the Blue Gate and the Dam Battlegrounds map.

Gaining access to this room allows Raiders to find items inside. You can obtain this keycard by searching containers, especially Breachable Containers, which are found across various maps. Raiders have reported finding it most often in the Buried City map, but also in the Dam Battlegrounds map, Spaceport map, Stella Montis map, and Blue Gate map. It is also available during the Night Raid event.

data.name: Roots
data.description: May be worth a few coins.
data.article: Roots are a crafting material used in various projects in ARC Raiders. They can commonly be found under trees and around bushes as well as valleys near broken trees. Check various Metaforge Maps to see where players are finding Roots more commonly.

data.name: Rope
data.description: Used in crafting.
data.article: Rope is a rare crafting material. You can use it at a Utility Station to craft utility items. Additionally, it can be recycled to gain crafting materials. Raiders can obtain Rope by scavenging in Residential and Commercial areas, or by purchasing it from Celeste.

data.name: Rosary
data.description: May be worth a few coins.
data.article: The Rosary is a collectible item that holds value. Raiders can sell it for coins or recycle it to obtain other resources. It shares its category with similar items such as a Rubber Duck, Silver Teaspoon Set, Statuette, Torn Book, or Vase.

data.name: Rotary Encoder
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Rotary Encoder is a rare item that Raiders can recycle into useful crafting materials. It is also required to complete the quest With a View. You can find Rotary Encoders by scavenging within the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Rubber Bands
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

data.name: Rubber Duck
data.description: Always there to lend an ear, should you need it.
data.article: The Rubber Duck is a common trinket that offers both a way to personalize your personal space and a practical use during your raids. You can collect these ducks and place them in your stash to decorate your Raider Den, making your base feel more like home. In the field, you can throw it to create a sound, effectively distracting nearby ARCs. This can be a useful tactic to draw attention away from your position or to lure them into a more favorable engagement area. You can find these trinkets inside chimneys when the Bird City event is active.

data.name: Rubber Pad
data.description: Can be recycled into rubber parts.
data.article: A Rubber Pad is a material intended for recycling into crafting materials. Its main purpose is to be processed at the Refiner. The resulting materials are used in crafting various components for mechanical and electrical projects.

data.name: Rubber Parts
data.description: Used to craft a wide range of items.
data.article: Rubber Parts are a basic crafting material essential for creating a wide array of useful items. You can find Rubber Parts by searching through mechanical, industrial, and electrical areas across the maps. They can also be obtained by recycling salvage. Furthermore, this material is sometimes available for purchase from Celeste, a vendor.

data.name: Ruined Accordion
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Ruined Accordion is a rare item Raiders can find while scavenging. Its main purpose is to be recycled, providing general crafting materials. These materials are helpful for creating various items and for different upgrades, which aids Raider progression. You typically obtain this item by exploring and searching containers or other points of interest in various areas of the map.

data.name: Ruined Augment
data.description: An augment ruined beyond repair.
data.article: The Ruined Augment is an augment that is too damaged to be equipped or used. Its primary purpose is to be recycled, providing useful crafting materials. This item is obtained exclusively by looting knocked-out Raiders. Augments degrade when their owner is knocked out, losing 30% durability with each instance. It becomes a Ruined Augment after its owner has been knocked out four times.

data.name: Ruined Baton
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Ruined Baton is an uncommon, damaged item. Similar to Ruined Handcuffs or Ruined Parachute, it serves as a component that can be recycled for various resources or sold for coins. Raiders also keep this item for use in crafting projects.

data.article: Ruined Handcuffs are a damaged item. They can be sold for coins or recycled into other general resources. Similar items that serve this purpose include the Ruined Parachute and Ruined Riot Shield.

data.name: Ruined Parachute
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Ruined Parachute is a resource Raiders can use as a source for crafting materials. Its main purpose is to be recycled, which breaks it down into various resources. These resources are useful for creating other items and supplies that help Raiders as they explore and progress.

data.name: Ruined Riot Shield
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Ruined Riot Shield is a non-functional piece of equipment that Raiders can discover in the game world. Its primary purpose is to be recycled, which transforms it into useful crafting materials for other projects. Raiders can obtain this item by scavenging within various security areas they encounter while exploring.

data.name: Ruined Tactical Vest
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Ruined Tactical Vest is an uncommon item that Raiders can recycle to obtain crafting materials. When recycled, it yields 550 coins.

data.name: Rusted Bolts
data.description: Can be recycled into metal parts.
data.article: Rusted Bolts are an uncommon item. Their primary purpose is to be recycled, providing crafting materials. Raiders can obtain these bolts by searching specific locations while exploring the different maps. They are often associated with projects like the Trophy Cabinet Project Headwinds.

data.name: Rusted Gear
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
Rusted Gear is a rare resource in ARC Raiders used for Gunsmith upgrade. Rusted Gears spawn primarily inside vehicles with intact hoods and industrial containers across all maps.

Best Rusted Gear Farming Locations:

  • Dam Battlegrounds — The Controlled Access Zone currently has the highest Rusted Gear spawn rate in the game. Also check the buses and cars next to northern extract and service trucks in the Scrapyard.

  • Blue Gate — Checkpoint and Underground garage beneath the warehouse packed with searchable vehicles.

  • Spaceport — Focus on rocket assembly and vehicle maintenance areas.

  • Stella Montis — Green breachable containers in the Loading Bay.

Tips to Maximize Rusted Gear Drops: Prioritize zones tagged "Industrial" on the map. Breach vehicles with closed hoods. Run night raids for higher spawn rates and better loot quality.

data.name: Rusted Shut Medical Kit
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
The Rusted Shut Medical Kit is a damaged version of a Medical Kit. Its rusted and shut state indicates it is not functional as a regular healing item.

Raiders obtain this item from loot or as a quest reward.

data.name: Rusted Tools
data.description: Can be recycled into metal parts.
data.article: Rusted Tools are rare items primarily used to upgrade your Gunsmith, which helps improve your crafting capabilities. These tools can also be recycled into crafting resources. You can obtain them by scavenging from containers.

data.name: Rusty ARC Steel
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: Rusty ARC Steel is a material that Raiders collect to use in recycling. It is a worn-out version of ARC Performance Steel. To find Rusty ARC Steel, you need to defeat different types of ARCs or search through the remains of ARCs that have already been destroyed. When you recycle this item, you will obtain general crafting components and coins.

data.name: Sample Cleaner
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Sample Cleaner provides useful resources. Its main use is to be recycled into crafting materials. You can find Sample Cleaners by scavenging in the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Secret Meeting Info

data.name: Seed Vault Box Key
data.description: A key opening a specific box in Stella Montis' Seed Vault.

data.name: Seeker Grenade
data.description: A homing grenade that targets a single nearby ARC dealing explosive damage on impact.
data.article:
The Seeker Grenade is a throwable item that automatically finds and targets a single nearby ARC, exploding upon impact to deal damage. It is useful for taking down smaller flying ARCs like Wasps, Hornets, Fireflies, and Snitches.

Raiders can obtain this grenade by crafting it at an Explosives Station using the Seeker Grenade Blueprint. It can also be purchased from the vendor Apollo. It functions as a smaller version of the Wolfpack.

data.name: Seeker Grenade Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Seeker Grenade
data.article: The Seeker Grenade Blueprint is a blueprint that unlocks the ability to craft seeker grenades at the Refiner, providing you with more options for dealing with ARCs during your raids.

data.name: Sensors
data.description: Used in crafting.
data.article: Sensors are a material primarily used in crafting at stations like the Explosives Station and Utility Station. They are also needed for certain projects. You can obtain Sensors by looting arcs such as the Snitch and Surveyor, and by looting Androids. They are also found by scavenging from Server Rack containers. Additionally, Sensors are available for purchase from Celeste using coins, or by recycling salvage.

data.name: Sentinel Firing Core
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Sentinel Firing Core is a Rare component salvaged from ARCs. Its primary use is as a crafting material for upgrading your Gunsmith station from level 2 to level 3. You can obtain this item by looting arcs like the Sentinel and the Courier. This item can also be recycled for crafting materials.

data.name: Sextant
data.description: Once thought to be a rudimentary spaceship prototype, it is claimed by the Nomads to be a sophisticated method for documenting one’s travels.

data.name: Shaker
data.description: A rhythmic instrument used to attract ARC's attention, and impress other Raiders.
data.article:
The Shaker is an Uncommon Gadget that plays one of two melodies. It is used to attract ARCs or to play music with other Raiders who have instruments like the Recorder or Acoustic Guitar. Using it prevents actions that require both hands.

You can obtain the Shaker in a few ways:

  • Craft it using crafting materials (requires the "Traveling Tinkerer" Inventory Skill).
  • Find it by scavenging in residential areas.
  • Purchase it from Shani for 40 coins (limit of three per day).
  • Get it from specific Raider Decks, such as the Raider Deck AR/RD 002: Goalie.

You can repair the Shaker with crafting materials or recycle it for resources.

data.name: Sheet Metal
data.description: Used in crafting.

data.name: Shield Recharger
data.description: A handheld kit that gradually recharges shield over time.
data.article:
The Shield Recharger is a handheld kit used to gradually restore your shield over time. When activated, it recharges 4 shield points per second for 10 seconds, adding up to 40 shield points in total. This amount is enough to fully replenish a Light Shield.

Raiders can craft a Shield Recharger at Workbench, which requires a Medical Lab to be unlocked. Alternatively, it can be crafted directly in your inventory if you have the 'In-Round Crafting' skill. It can also be purchased from Lance for 1,560 coins.

data.name: Shield Stress Testing
data.description: Sustained damage could reveal exactly what makes a shield give out—and how to make that happen faster. For science, naturally.

data.name: Shotgun Ammo
data.description: Shotgun shells used for shotguns.
data.article:
Shotgun Ammo is a type of ammunition used exclusively by shotguns. It helps penetrate ARC armor more easily than light ammo, but it is not as effective as medium ammo.

Raiders can obtain Shotgun Ammo in several ways:

  • By scavenging or finding it in Raider Caches.
  • By looting arcs.
  • It can be crafted at the Workbench.
  • It is also sold by Tian Wen.

data.name: Shotgun Choke I
data.description: Slightly reduces base dispersion.

data.name: Shotgun Choke II
data.description: Moderately reduces base dispersion.
data.article:
Shotgun Choke II is a Weapon Mod that reduces how much shotgun pellets spread when fired. Attaching this mod makes your shotgun shots land in a tighter pattern, helping you hit targets more accurately.

You can obtain Shotgun Choke II by scavenging it in the environment, crafting it at a Gunsmith with the Shotgun Choke II Blueprint, or purchasing it from Tian Wen. It can be recycled to gain resources.

data.name: Shotgun Choke II Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Shotgun Choke II
data.article: The Shotgun Choke II Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Shotgun Choke II weapon modification at the Gunsmith. This modification helps improve shotguns by reducing how much their shots spread.

data.name: Shotgun Choke III
data.description: Significantly reduces base dispersion.
data.article: The Shotgun Choke III is an attachment for shotguns that helps make your shots spread less, increasing their accuracy. It also makes the weapon last longer before needing repairs. You can craft it at a Gunsmith bench once you have the Shotgun Choke III Blueprint.

data.name: Shotgun Choke III Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Shotgun Choke III
data.article: The Shotgun Choke III Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft a weapon mod at the Gunsmith bench level 3. This mod helps shotguns fire pellets in a tighter pattern, making their shots more focused.

data.name: Shotgun Silencer
data.description: Moderately reduces the amount of noise produced when firing.
data.article:
The Shotgun Silencer is a weapon modification that moderately reduces the noise your shotgun makes when fired. It specifically reduces sound by 50%, making your shots quieter. This modification can be used with shotguns.

You can craft it at a Gunsmith bench using a Shotgun Silencer Blueprint. It can also be recycled or salvaged to recover other resources.

data.name: Shotgun Silencer Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Shotgun Silencer. Moderately reduces the amount of noise produced when firing.
data.article: The Shotgun Silencer Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Shotgun Silencer at the Gunsmith. This weapon modification is designed to reduce the amount of noise your shotgun makes when fired and is compatible with shotguns. The blueprint itself can be recycled for resources.

data.name: Showstopper
data.description: A grenade that detonates after a delay, stunning enemies within its radius.
data.article: The Showstopper is a type of grenade that stuns ARCs and other Raiders within its blast area. It detonates after a short delay or immediately upon hitting a target. You can find this item by scavenging, or by crafting it at an Explosives Station. Crafting requires you to first learn the Showstopper Blueprint.

data.name: Showstopper Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Showstopper.
data.article: The Showstopper Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Showstopper grenade at an Explosives Station. This grenade is designed to stun ARCs and other Raiders within its blast radius of 6 meters. It detonates after a 3.5-second delay, stunning ARCs for 7 seconds and Raiders for 2 seconds.

data.name: Shrapnel Grenade
data.description: A makeshift fuze grenade that bursts into razor-sharp fragments upon detonation.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating.
data.article: The Shrapnel Grenade is a throwable item that explodes, scattering razor-sharp fragments. It deals damage to those caught in its blast, but it is less effective against the armor of ARCs. You can get this grenade by scavenging or by crafting it at an Explosives Station level 2. It can also be recycled to recover various materials.

data.name: Shredder Gyro
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

guide_links.label: Deal Damage to Shredders: Weekly Trial

data.article: A Shredder Gyro is a component scavenged from defeated Shredders, a type of ARC. This item plays a role in crafting and maintaining your gear. You can use it as a component when crafting at a Gunsmith. It is also needed to repair weapons, helping to keep them in good condition. Furthermore, Shredder Gyros are required for various projects and can be recycled into salvage.

data.name: Signal Amplifier
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Signal Amplifier is a useful resource item primarily used for its component parts. Its main role is to provide crafting materials when you recycle it, which are essential for making different items. You can find Signal Amplifiers by scavenging inside containers, which are commonly located across Stella Montis.

data.name: Silencer I
data.description: Slightly reduces the amount of noise produced when firing.
data.article: The Silencer I is a weapon modification that reduces the sound your weapon makes when fired. This item is crafted at the Gunsmith once you have the Silencer I Blueprint.

data.name: Silencer I Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Silencer I
data.article: The Silencer I Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Silencer I weapon mod at a Gunsmith Bench level 2. This mod helps reduce the amount of noise your weapon makes when you fire it. The blueprint itself can be recycled for coins and other resources.

To obtain this mod, you must first find its Silencer II Blueprint, which can be crafted at a Gunsmith bench. It can also be recycled or salvaged to recover general resources and components.

data.name: Silencer II Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Silencer II
data.article: The Silencer II Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft a Silencer II weapon mod at a Gunsmith Bench. This mod helps reduce the sound your weapon makes when firing.

data.article: The Silencer III is a weapon modification that makes your shots much quieter. This modification reduces the noise your weapon makes by 60%, helping you remain hidden from ARCs during combat. While it offers quieter firing, it also causes your weapon to wear out 20% faster. It is compatible with many weapons, including the Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Anvil, Arpeggio, Burletta, Osprey, Renegade, Torrente, Venator, Bettina, Bobcat, and Tempest. You can recycle it to obtain other resources.

data.name: Silver Teaspoon Set
data.description: A shining, shimmering set of refinement and elegance.
data.article: The Silver Teaspoon Set is considered a valuable item, often described as showing refinement and elegance. It helps Raiders progress by being sold to Traders for coins, which are essential for various purchases and upgrades. Trinkets like this set are also frequently used to complete different projects.

data.name: Simple Gun Parts
data.description: Used to craft weapons.
data.article:
Simple Gun Parts are a common material for crafting, upgrading, and repairing many types of weapons. They can also be refined into more specialized components at a Refiner. These parts are used in crafting various items at a Gunsmith or Workbench.

You can find Simple Gun Parts by scavenging or by salvaging them from defeated ARCs including Wasps, Hornets, Turrets, Sentinels, and Shredders. They can also be bought from the vendor Celeste or obtained by recycling other materials.

data.name: "Sirena Dorata" Ship Model
data.description: With the Mediterranean sun glistening off its hull, this vibrant yacht is the timeless epitome of saltwater splendour.
data.article: The "Sirena Dorata" Ship Model is a decorative item found within the game. It serves as a collectible that Raiders can discover.

data.name: Skulker Driver
data.description: Drops from Meerkat.

data.name: Skulker Targeter
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

data.name: Smoke Grenade
data.description: A grenade that creates a lingering smoke cloud on impact, blocking visibility from ARC and other Raiders.
data.article:
A Smoke Grenade is a throwable item that releases a thick smoke cloud on impact. This cloud blocks the sight of ARCs and other Raiders, providing a way to escape or approach unseen. It lasts for 20 seconds and covers a 7.5-meter radius.

You can craft this item at a Workbench or Utility Station once you have learned the smoke grenade blueprint and gathered the necessary crafting materials. Apollo also sells the Smoke Grenade for 3,000 coins, with a daily limit of 6.

data.name: Smoke Grenade Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Smoke Grenade
data.article: A Smoke Grenade Blueprint allows you to craft smoke grenades at a Workbench or Utility Station, which create a cloud to block visibility from ARCs and other Raiders. It can be found by looting containers in Buried City as well as other maps during Night Raid or Cold Snap game types.

data.name: Smoke Grenade Trap
data.description: A laser trip wire that detonates a Smoke Grenade.
data.article:
A Smoke Grenade Trap is a device that projects a visible red laser up to five meters. When its laser beam is interrupted, it detonates a Smoke Grenade, releasing a thick gray smoke cloud. This smoke helps to hide Raider movements and obstructs the view of both ARCs and other Raiders.

You can place this device on almost any surface, but its laser is clearly visible to everyone. If a trap has not yet detonated, the Raider who placed it can disarm and pick it up.

This trap is crafted at the Workbench, requiring certain components and the "Traveling Tinkerer" skill.

data.name: Snap Blast Grenade
data.description: A grenade that sticks to surfaces, dealing explosive damage after a short delay.
data.article:
The Snap Blast Grenade is a magnetic grenade that sticks to surfaces before exploding after a short delay, dealing explosive damage. It is used in the Sparks Fly quest.

You can find this item in several ways:

  • By scavenging.
  • From containers such as Raider Caches, Security Lockers, and Weapon Cases.
  • By purchasing from Apollo for 2,400 coins, with a daily limit of 3.

This grenade can be crafted at an Explosives Station. It can also be recycled for resources.

data.name: Snap Hook
data.description: A gadget that allows the user to scale structures and cover large distances.
data.article: The Snap Hook is a gadget that helps you move quickly across areas by grappling to higher ground or managing descents. You can get a Snap Hook by completing the Lost In Transmission quest. It can also be crafted at a Utility Station once you have learned the Snap Hook Blueprint. Additionally, Snap Hooks are rewarded from certain Projects, such as Stage 5 of the Trophy Display. You can also find them listed in Raider Deck AR/RD 001: Ryder & Voyager and Raider Deck AR/RD 002: Goalie.

data.name: Snap Hook Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Snap Hook
data.article:
The Snap Hook Blueprint is a blueprint that teaches you how to build the Snap Hook, which allows you to move quickly across distances or reach higher spots. Once learned, you can craft it at a Utility Station.

You can find this blueprint during Electromagnetic Storm map condition on various maps, most commonly in Residential loot areas.

data.name: Snitch Scanner
data.description: Can be recycled into ARC Alloy.

guide_links.label: Damage Flying-based ARC Enemies: Weekly Trial

data.article:
The Snitch Scanner is a utility item you can throw to call in Wasps. Once thrown, it becomes damaged.

You obtain this item by defeating Snitches, which are a type of ARC enemy.

It is used to upgrade your Utility Station and is also an item needed to complete The Trifecta quest. Additionally, you can recycle it for salvage.

data.name: Snowball
data.description: A compact snowball fashioned out of the most malleable and aerodynamic snow.

guide_links.label: Throw Snowballs at Bastions: Weekly Trial
Throw Snowballs at Rocketeers: Weekly Trial

data.article: A Snowball is a compact, throwable item fashioned from malleable and aerodynamic snow. It deals minor damage and can be used to complete various tasks or Weekly Trials, such as throwing them at Rocketeers. Raiders obtain Snowballs by collecting them from Snow Piles. These piles appear on maps when the Cold Snap map modifier is active.

data.name: Solid-Core Casting Tech
data.description: Shotgun engagements against drones offer a useful test of stopping power. Concentrating the full charge into a single projectile could produce far more decisive results.

data.name: Spaceport Container Storage Key
data.description: Unlocks a door in the Container Storage in Spaceport
data.article: The Spaceport Container Storage Key is a key used to open specific locked doors. Its primary use is to unlock one of three doors found on the east side of the Container Storage area in the Spaceport map. These particular doors are located on the top floor of the Container Storage. You can find this key while exploring the map, or by completing the quest called Switching The Supply.

data.name: Spaceport Control Tower Key
data.description: Unlocks a door in Control Tower A6 in Spaceport
data.article: The Spaceport Control Tower Key is an access item that allows you to open a specific locked area. Its main purpose is to unlock the Control Tower in the Spaceport map, which Raiders often seek for its contents. It functions similarly to the Blue Gate Communication Tower Key, providing entry to an otherwise inaccessible tower.

data.name: Spaceport Trench Tower Key
data.description: Unlocks a door to the Trench Towers in Spaceport
data.article: The Spaceport Trench Tower Key is a specific key used to open secured trench tower buildings located within the Spaceport map. This key allows Raiders to access areas that might contain valuable items or provide a way to complete objectives. It is sometimes also referred to as a Spaceport Control Tower Key, indicating its purpose in granting entry to these fortified structures.

data.name: Spaceport Warehouse Key
data.description: Unlocks a door in the Shipping Warehouse in Spaceport
data.article: The Spaceport Warehouse Key is a key that allows you to open a specific set of locked doors. These doors are found on the North side of the Shipping Warehouse, located on the Second Floor of the Spaceport map.

data.name: Speaker Component
data.description: Used in crafting.
data.article:
A Speaker Component is a resource used for crafting various utility items. You can use it at a Utility Station or with the 'Traveling Tinkerer' Inventory Skill to create different helpful items. This component can also be recycled into other resources.

You can obtain Speaker Components in several ways:

  • Scavenged from containers or the environment.
  • Obtained by recycling or salvaging other items.
  • Purchased directly from Celeste.

data.name: Spectrometer
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Spectrometer is a rare item. Its primary use is to be recycled into crafting materials that can then be used in various projects. You can find this item by scavenging throughout the environment in the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Spectrum Analyzer
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Spectrum Analyzer is used to obtain valuable crafting materials. Its primary purpose is to be recycled into general materials that help you make other items. Raiders can find it by scavenging in the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Spotter Relay
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
The Spotter Relay is used to progress the Trophy Display Project. When deployed, it functions as a trap that lures nearby ARCs. It is a key component for Stage 2 of the Trophy Display Project and is also needed for the quest Combat Recon. You can track all project needs on the Needed Items Tracker.

Obtain Spotter Relays by destroying Spotter Drones, which only spawn when a Bombardier ARC is active nearby. They are found on Spaceport and Buried City maps, but the north-west section of the Blue Gate map offers the most consistent encounters.

data.name: Spring Cushion
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Spring Cushion can be broken down into useful components. Its main purpose is to provide general crafting materials when you recycle it. You can find this item by searching containers like trash cans, which are commonly located in Residential and Commercial areas.

data.name: Stable Stock I
data.description: Slightly improves dispersion & recoil recovery time.
data.article: Stable Stock I is a weapon mod. It helps Raiders manage how much their weapon kicks back after firing and how spread out their shots are.

data.name: Stable Stock II
data.description: Moderately improves dispersion & recoil recovery time.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Arpeggio, Il Toro, Osprey, Renegade, Torrente, Bettina, Bobcat, Tempest, Vulcano, Aphelion

data.article:
The Stable Stock II is a weapon modification that helps make your weapon more stable. It allows your weapon to recover faster after you fire and reduces how much your shots spread.

To obtain this item, craft it at a Gunsmith Bench level 1 using a Stable Stock II Blueprint.

data.name: Stable Stock II Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Stable Stock II
data.article: The Stable Stock II Blueprint is a blueprint that teaches you how to craft the Stable Stock II weapon modification at a Gunsmith. Once learned, it improves how your gun handles by making it recover faster from recoil and spread. This blueprint can be found through scavenging, often appearing in Raider Containers across any map. It can also be obtained as a reward for completing quests or by succeeding in trials.

data.name: Stable Stock III
data.description: Significantly improves dispersion & recoil recovery time.
data.article:
The Stable Stock III is a Weapon Mod that greatly improves how quickly your weapon becomes steady again after recoil and how fast its accuracy returns after shooting. Keep in mind that attaching this mod will slightly increase the time it takes to ready your weapon and put it away.

You can craft this mod at a Gunsmith bench, but you will need to have the Stable Stock III Blueprint first.

data.name: Stable Stock III Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Stable Stock III
data.article:
The Stable Stock III Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Stable Stock III weapon modification at a Gunsmith Bench. This modification improves weapon handling by reducing shot spread and recoil recovery time.

You can find this blueprint:

  • Inside containers like Boxes, Ammo Crates, Breachable Containers, and Lockers.
  • Across maps such as the Spaceport, Blue Gate, Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, and Riven Tides.
  • During events including Cold Snap, Electromagnetic Storm, Night Raid, Hurricane, and Locked Gate.

Recycling the blueprint yields coins.

data.name: Stack of Movie Tapes
data.description: A stack of movie tapes, sure to please even the most pedantic of cinephiles.
data.article: A Stack of Movie Tapes is a special item Raiders might carry in their inventory when participating in certain game events. It is linked to events such as the Flickering Flames Event and the Movie Night quest. During these events, Raiders typically collect items, and the Stack of Movie Tapes likely represents their progress or completion of these event-related tasks.

data.name: Statuette
data.description: Worth a small fortune.
data.article: The Statuette is a small trinket. Its main purpose is to be sold for coins, offering a good amount of value. You can find Statuettes by scavenging in areas like Old World Residential.

data.name: Steel Cable
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

data.name: Steel Spring
data.description: Used to craft a wide range of items. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: Steel Spring is a material used in crafting. Its main purpose is to create various weapon modifications at the Gunsmith bench and other components at the Refiner. It is also a necessary component to complete the Expedition project. You can find Steel Spring by scavenging in the environment or by opening Metal Crates. It can also be purchased from Celeste.

data.name: Stella Montis Archives Key
data.description: Unlocks a door in the Archives in Stella Montis
data.article: The Stella Montis Archives Key is a key used to unlock the Archives area found within the Stella Montis map. This key provides access to a specific, otherwise restricted section of the map, allowing Raiders to explore it.

data.name: Stella Montis Assembly Admin Key
data.description: Unlocks a door in Assembly in Stella Montis
data.article: The Stella Montis Assembly Admin Key is a key used to unlock a specific door within the Assembly area of the Stella Montis map. Raiders use this key to access new sections of the map that are otherwise inaccessible. It can be carried one at a time, weighs 0.25kg, and has a value of 100 coins.

data.name: Stella Montis Medical Storage Key
data.description: Unlocks a door in Medical Research in Stella Montis
data.article: The Stella Montis Medical Storage Key is a key used to unlock the Medical Storage door located within the Stella Montis map. Gaining entry to this storage typically allows Raiders to find helpful resources or items inside.

data.name: Stella Montis Security Checkpoint Key
data.description: Unlocks a door in the Security Checkpoint in Stella Montis
data.article: The Stella Montis Security Checkpoint Key is a key used to open security checkpoints within the Stella Montis map. Raiders use this key to gain access to areas that are otherwise locked by these checkpoints.

data.article: The Sterilized Bandage is a medical item that gradually restores a large amount of health over time. Raiders can craft this item at the Medical Lab.
