data.description: Has a good damage output, but has a low fire-rate for an SMG, and can be hard to control.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Stitcher I is a fully-automatic Submachine Gun that uses light ammo. Raiders might receive this weapon when choosing a Free Loadout, or they can find it by scavenging. It can also be crafted at the Workbench once Gunsmith is available, or purchased from Tian Wen. It can be used to craft improved versions and can also be recycled for resources.

data.name: Stitcher II
data.description: Has a good damage output, but has a low fire-rate for an SMG, and can be hard to control.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Stitcher II is a fully-automatic Submachine Gun that uses light ammo. It is an improved version of the Stitcher I, offering less horizontal recoil, faster reload speed, and increased durability.

Raiders can craft the Stitcher II at a Gunsmith Bench by combining one Stitcher I with salvage materials. It can also be obtained as part of a Free Loadout or purchased from Tian Wen. The weapon sells for 2,000 coins.

data.name: Stitcher III
data.description: Has a good damage output, but has a low fire-rate for an SMG, and can be hard to control.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Stitcher III is an upgraded fully-automatic submachine gun that improves upon the Stitcher II. It offers better weapon control with reduced horizontal recoil, faster reload times, and improved durability compared to its previous version. Raiders primarily obtain this weapon by crafting it at a Gunsmith from other components. It can be recycled for useful materials and resources.

data.name: Stitcher IV
data.description: Has a good damage output, but has a low fire-rate for an SMG, and can be hard to control.
data.flavor_text: Weak against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Stitcher IV is an advanced, fully-automatic submachine gun that uses light ammo. It is an improved version of the Stitcher III, offering enhanced combat performance. This weapon provides significantly reduced horizontal recoil, faster reload times, and increased durability, making it more reliable in engagements. It can be crafted at the Gunsmith Bench level 1. If no longer needed, it can be recycled for valuable resources or sold for 5,000 coins.

data.name: Succulent (Backpack Charm)
data.description: Complete the quest The Root Of The Matter to get this charm.
data.article: The Succulent (Backpack Charm) is a cosmetic item used to customize your Raider's appearance. It attaches to the bottom of your backpack and swings as you move, adding a unique visual detail. To get this charm, you need to complete the The Root Of The Matter quest.

data.name: Surge Coil
data.description: A deployable device that periodically electrifies the area around itself and briefly stuns anything caught within it.
data.article: The Surge Coil is a deployable device that periodically electrifies the area around itself, briefly stunning anything caught within it. It also causes ARCs to redirect their attention towards it, much like a Lure Grenade. This item can be found by scavenging or crafted at the Explosives Station once you have learned its Surge Coil Blueprint. The blueprint can be obtained by looting arcs.

data.name: Surge Coil Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Surge Coil.
data.article:
The Surge Coil Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Surge Coil, a deployable device that electrifies the area around it. When placed, it periodically sends out an electric pulse that briefly stuns both ARCs and other Raiders who come too close. This can be useful for controlling areas, buying extra time during combat or looting, and escaping fast-moving ARCs like Shredders.

You can find the Surge Coil Blueprint by looting various containers, such as lockers, desk drawers, cupboards, and industrial crates, during the Electromagnetic Storm map condition. You must be in a map where this condition is active. Check the Event Timers to see when the Electromagnetic Storm is running on any map. It has been reported to drop in areas like the Testing Annex, Water Treatment Facility, and Hydroponic Domes within the Dam Battlegrounds, among others.

data.name: Surge Shield Recharger
data.description: A handheld kit that recharges a shield on use.
data.article: The Surge Shield Recharger is a handheld kit used to instantly restore 50 shield charge after a brief moment, which helps you stay protected during engagements. This item is crafted at a Medical Lab using other resources.

data.name: Surveyor Vault
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: A Surveyor Vault is a rare item used to improve your crafting abilities and complete certain projects. You will need it to upgrade your Medical Lab to level 3, which is a station found in your Hideout. It is also a requirement for the first stage of the Trophy Display project. You can obtain Surveyor Vaults by looting arcs such as the Surveyor or Courier. Additionally, you can recycle them to gain crafting materials or salvage them for resources.

data.name: Synthesized Fuel
data.description: Used to craft utility items and explosives. Can be recycled into chemicals.
data.article: Synthesized Fuel is a material used to craft explosives and other helpful items. You can also throw it, and if it gets shot, it will explode, causing damage in a small area. This material is also important for improving your Explosives Station level 1. You can find Synthesized Fuel by scavenging in the environment or by recycling other items. Additionally, Celeste sells a limited amount of Synthesized Fuel each day for coins. If you have extra, you can recycle it to get various resources.

data.name: Syringe
data.description: Used to craft medical supplies. Can be recycled into plastic.
data.article:
A Syringe is a sterile item used to craft medical supplies and is also required for the Doctor's Orders quest.

Raiders can find Syringes in containers such as bags and medical crates across Buried City, Dam Battlegrounds, Blue Gate, and Stella Montis. The trader Celeste also sells them in Dam Battlegrounds for coins. Alternatively, you can obtain a Syringe by recycling salvage.

When no longer needed, a Syringe can be recycled into crafting materials.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 1
data.description: Basic tactical augment. More Quick Use slots for more tactical choice, but limited survivability and slightly lower looting potential.
data.article:
The Tactical Mk. 1 is an Augment that adds more Quick Use slots, allowing you to carry more tactical items. While it offers five Quick Use slots and compatibility with a medium shield, it has fewer backpack slots and a lower maximum weight capacity.

You can get the Tactical Mk. 1 in a few ways. Lance offers it as a free exchange if you provide a Free Loadout Augment, or you can purchase it from him directly. It can also be crafted at a Gear Bench. Additionally, you might find this Augment by scavenging.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 2
data.description: Adds more backpack space and an extra utility item slot.
data.flavor_text: Upon Shield break, deploys a small smoke grenade. Has a fixed cooldown.
data.article: The Tactical Mk. 2 is a type of Augment that increases your backpack space and provides an additional slot for utility items. It also has a unique ability: if your shield breaks, it automatically deploys a small smoke grenade after a short cooldown. This augment is an improved version of the Tactical Mk. 1. You can craft it at a Gear Bench, and it can be repaired or recycled into general resources.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Defensive)
data.description: A defense-focused augment for keeping Shields topped up.
data.flavor_text: Allows Shield Rechargers to be used while running.
data.article:
The Tactical Mk.3 (Defensive) is an augment designed to help Raiders keep their shields full. Its main feature is a built-in shield recharger, which allows you to recharge your shields even while running. This augment also works with light, medium, and heavy shields, offering broad compatibility.

This augment can be crafted at Gear Bench once its blueprint has been learned. Blueprints for it can be found through scavenging. It can also be recycled into other resources or repaired.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Defensive) Blueprint
data.description: a defense-focused augment for keeping Shields topped up
data.article: The Tactical MK.3 (Defensive) Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Tactical Mk.3 (Defensive) augment at a Gear Bench. It helps keep your shields full, letting you use a Shield Recharger even while running.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Healing)
data.description: A healing-focused augment which adds extra slots for healing items.
data.flavor_text: When revived from being downed, releases a healing cloud that restores 20 health over 10 seconds. Has a 30-second cooldown.
data.article:
The Tactical Mk. 3 (Healing) is a tactical augment designed to improve a Raider's healing capabilities. It provides additional slots for carrying healing items in both your backpack and safe pockets. When you are revived after being downed, it releases a healing cloud that instantly restores 45 health to you and nearby Raiders. This ability has a 45-second cooldown.

This augment's Blueprint is found by participating in the Locked Gate event. Once you have the Blueprint, you can craft it at a Gear Bench. The augment can also be recycled to recover general resources.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Healing) Blueprint
data.description: A healing-focused augment which adds extra slots for healing items.
data.article: The Tactical MK.3 (Healing) Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft a specialized augment designed for healing at Gear Bench. When equipped, the augment provides more capacity for healing items and, upon being revived from a downed state, creates a healing cloud that instantly restores 45 health. This effect has a 45-second cooldown. It can also be recycled for resources or salvaged for components.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Revival)
data.description: A tactical augment focused on utility over defense and looting.
data.flavor_text: Restores 1 health every 5 seconds. When damage is taken, the effect is paused for 30 seconds.
data.article:
The Tactical Mk. 3 (Revival) is an Augment that helps Raiders stay in the fight and support their teammates. It provides a slow regeneration, restoring 1 health every 5 seconds, though this effect pauses for 30 seconds if you take damage. This Augment also comes with an integrated defibrillator, which has unlimited uses but requires a 240-second cooldown period after each revival.

It can be crafted at Gear Bench using the Tactical Mk. 3 (Revival) Blueprint. The blueprint itself can be obtained by participating in the Locked Gate event. Once crafted, it can be recycled to recover some general resources.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Revival) Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft Tactical MK. 3 (Revival) Blueprint.
data.article: The Tactical Mk. 3 (Revival) Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Tactical Mk. 3 (Revival) augment at a Gear Bench. It comes with an integrated defibrillator, offering a utility option for use during raids. You can obtain this blueprint by participating in the Locked Gate event.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Smoke)
data.description: An upgraded version of the Tactical MK. 2 augment, adding expanded capacity across the board.
data.article: The Tactical Mk. 3 (Smoke) is an augment that automatically deploys a small smoke grenade when your shield breaks, providing a defensive cover. It is an improved version of the Tactical Mk. 2 augment, offering more capacity. This augment can be used with Light and Medium shields. You can obtain this item by scavenging in the environment or by crafting it at a Gear Bench once you have learned its blueprint. It has a maximum loadout weight of 50.0.

data.name: Tactical Mk. 3 (Smoke) Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a T3 Smoke Augment
data.article: The Tactical MK.3 (Smoke) Blueprint is a blueprint used to craft the Tactical Mk. 3 (Smoke) augment at a Gear Bench. It automatically deploys a small smoke grenade when your shield breaks, which can provide momentary cover.

data.name: Tagging Grenade
data.description: A grenade that detonates after a delay, tagging Raiders and ARC enemies in an area, allowing you to briefly track their location.
data.article:
The Tagging Grenade is a utility item that helps you locate ARCs and other Raiders. When thrown, it detonates after a short delay, revealing the positions of ARCs and other Raiders within a 6-meter area for 30 seconds. This allows you to track their movements, which can help you plan your next steps or avoid being surprised.

You can craft this grenade at the Utility Station once you have learned the Tagging Grenade Blueprint.

data.name: Tagging Grenade Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Tagging Grenade
data.article: The Tagging Grenade Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft Tagging Grenades at a Utility Station. Once thrown, it detonates to briefly reveal the locations of ARCs and other Raiders in its blast area.

data.name: Tangerine (Warden Color)
data.description: A new cosmetic variant will be added to your collection.
data.article: Tangerine (Warden Color) is a cosmetic item for your collection. It provides a new color choice for the Warden outfit, letting you change the appearance of your character's clothing.

data.name: Targeted Component Trial
data.description: Even the toughest machines have their weak spots. Consistent strikes against vulnerable components could reveal a way to develop rounds that hit them where it hurts most. Metaphorically speaking.

data.name: Tattered ARC Lining
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: Tattered ARC Lining is a material that was once an intact ARC Thermo Lining. Raiders use it for recycling into general crafting materials. You can obtain this item by scavenging the husks of ARCs.

data.name: Tattered Clothes
data.description: Can be recycled into fabric.
data.article: Tattered Clothes are an Uncommon item primarily used to gather essential crafting materials. You can recycle them to obtain various resources needed for different projects and upgrades. These clothes are typically found by scavenging through residential areas, rather than as drops from ARCs.

data.name: Telemetry Transceiver
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Telemetry Transceiver is primarily used for recycling into crafting materials. You can obtain it by scavenging inside containers, which are commonly found in the Stella Montis map, and sometimes also in the Dam Battlegrounds map. When recycled, it provides resources for crafting and a base value of 2250 coins.

data.name: Tellurion
data.description: A marvel of ancient ingenuity, those with a penchant for stargazing may find the mesmerizing patterns oddly familiar.

data.name: Tempest Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Tempest
data.article: The Tempest Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Tempest I assault rifle at a Gunsmith. You can obtain it by scavenging in the game world, and it has been found during 'Night Raid' events.

data.name: Tempest I
data.description: Has moderate fire rate and accuracy.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Tempest I is a fully-automatic assault rifle that uses medium ammo. It is a reliable weapon for engaging ARCs. Raiders can craft it at the Gunsmith Bench level 1 after acquiring and learning the Tempest Blueprint. It serves as the initial version of the Tempest weapon series.

data.name: Tempest II
data.description: Has moderate fire rate and accuracy.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Tempest II is an upgraded version of the Tempest I assault rifle. This fully-automatic weapon uses medium ammo and offers improved combat performance over its previous model. It provides reduced horizontal recoil, a faster reload time, and increased durability, while maintaining a moderate fire rate and accuracy. Raiders can obtain it by crafting at the Gunsmith, where a Tempest I is combined with various crafting materials.

data.name: Tempest III
data.description: Has moderate fire rate and accuracy.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Tempest III is an upgraded version of the Tempest II assault rifle, providing enhanced performance. This assault rifle uses medium ammo. When equipped, it offers a noticeable reduction in horizontal recoil and a faster reload speed compared to its previous versions. It also comes with improved durability, allowing for more shots before needing repairs. You can obtain it by upgrading a Tempest II at a Gunsmith bench. It can also be recycled for resources or sold for coins.

data.name: Tempest IV
data.description: Has moderate fire rate and accuracy.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Tempest IV is an advanced assault rifle, representing the highest upgrade level in the Tempest series. This fully-automatic weapon uses medium ammo and significantly improves a Raider's combat capabilities. It offers 50% reduced horizontal recoil, 40% reduced reload time, and increased durability compared to its previous versions.

Raiders obtain the Tempest IV by crafting it at a crafting station that meets the necessary requirements, which involves upgrading a Tempest III. It can be repaired using materials to restore its durability. It can also be sold for 27,000 coins.

data.name: Tether Launcher
data.description: A two-shot tether launcher that anchors a line to whatever it hits, linking both points together.

data.name: Tether Launcher Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Tether Launcher

data.name: Thermal Shaker
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.

data.name: Thermite-Tipped Rounds
data.description: Impact damage is useful. Setting the problem on fire afterward feels like a reasonable improvement.

data.name: Thermostat
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Thermostat is a resource that serves as a crafting material. Its main purpose is to be recycled, providing materials that are important for crafting various other items to help Raiders progress. You can typically find Thermostats by searching and collecting items from different spots located within Residential areas.

data.name: Tick Pod
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Tick Pod is an uncommon item obtained by defeating Ticks. This item is used in various crafting and upgrade processes at the Medical Lab and for upgrading the Medical Lab itself. Tick Pods are also required for a project at the Trophy Display. You can recycle them to obtain crafting materials.

data.name: Toaster
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Toaster is a rare item that serves two main purposes. It is used as a component when crafting advanced equipment at the Refiner, alongside other components. Alternatively, if not needed for crafting, it can be recycled to obtain general crafting materials.

data.name: Top Mounted Optics Retrofittings
data.description: Elevated firing positions provide clear sightlines. Osprey field data under those conditions could support development of improved magnification.

data.name: Torch Ginger
data.description: A plant used to craft medical supplies.
data.article: Torch Ginger is a plant used to craft medical supplies. If you choose to recycle it, you will lose 150 coins.

data.name: Torn Blanket
data.description: Can be recycled into fabric.
data.article: Torn Blanket is a material item that can be processed to obtain other resources. Its main use is to provide crafting components used to create various general supplies and other useful items. This item can be recycled to yield resources, or it can be salvaged for a smaller quantity.

data.name: Torn Book
data.description: What pages remain speak of chosen heroes, vampires, and lots of longing glances.
data.article: The Torn Book is a trinket, primarily used as a quest item. Raiders need this item to successfully complete the Cold Storage quest. Additionally, if you have no immediate need for it, the Torn Book can be sold for coins.

data.name: Torrente Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Torrente
data.article: The Torrente Blueprint is a blueprint that allows Raiders to craft the Torrente weapon.

data.name: Torrente I
data.description: Has a large ammo capacity, but is only accurate while crouched.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Torrente I is a fully-automatic light machine gun that uses medium ammo. This weapon has a large ammunition capacity and provides sustained fire, though it is most accurate when used while crouched. It offers moderate penetration against ARC armor during combat. Raiders craft this item at a Gunsmith after learning the Torrente I Blueprint. Once crafted, it can be further upgraded to more advanced versions or recycled for various resources.

data.name: Torrente II
data.description: Has a large ammo capacity, but is only accurate while crouched.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Torrente II is a fully-automatic Light Machine Gun (LMG) that uses medium ammo. It serves as an improved version of the Torrente I, offering a larger magazine size, faster reloading, and better durability for Raiders. This weapon is crafted at the Gunsmith by combining a Torrente I with other crafting materials.

data.name: Torrente III
data.description: Has a large ammo capacity, but is only accurate while crouched.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Torrente III is an upgraded Light Machine Gun (LMG) that uses medium ammo. This weapon has a large ammo capacity and is most accurate when the Raider is crouching. Compared to earlier versions, it provides an increased magazine size, a faster reload time, and improved durability, making it suitable for sustained combat.

Raiders can craft this LMG at Gunsmith. It can also be recycled for resources or repaired to restore its durability.

data.name: Torrente IV
data.description: Has a large ammo capacity, but is only accurate while crouched.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Torrente IV is an upgraded, fully-automatic Light Machine Gun that uses medium ammo. It is designed for sustained fire with a large ammo capacity. This version provides a significant increase to magazine size, a faster reload time, and improved durability compared to earlier Torrente models.

Raiders can craft it at a Gunsmith using crafting materials. It can also be recycled for resources.

data.name: Trailblazer
data.description: A grenade that emits a trail of flammable gas along its path, causing an explosive chain reaction when it ignites.
data.article:
The Trailblazer Grenade is a throwable item that releases a trail of flammable gas when used. After a moment, the gas ignites, causing an explosion.

Raiders can obtain this grenade in a few ways. It can be found by scavenging. You can also craft it at an Explosives Station level 1, which requires learning its blueprint and using various components. Additionally, it can be purchased from Apollo for 6,600 coins, with a limit of three per day. When no longer needed, it can be recycled for other resources.

data.name: Trailblazer Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Trailblazer Grenade
data.article: The Trailblazer Grenade Blueprint is a blueprint used at an Explosives Station level 1 to craft Trailblazer Grenades. They release a trail of flammable gas along their path, which then ignites and explodes after a short delay.

data.name: Train Model
data.description: Hand-crafted with full underbody detailing, these models offer a surprisingly intricate schematic of pre-Exodus locomotion.

data.name: Trigger 'Nade
data.description: A remote-detonated grenade that can stick to surfaces and ARC, dealing explosive damage when triggered.
data.article:
The Trigger 'Nade is a grenade you throw that sticks to surfaces and ARCs. It does not explode right away; instead, you trigger it remotely to cause an explosion that deals damage in an area.

To get this item, you first need its blueprint, which is given as a reward when you complete the Sparks Fly quest. Once you have it, you can craft this grenade at an Explosives Station.

data.name: Trigger Nade Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Trigger Nade
data.article: The Trigger Nade Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft trigger nades at the appropriate crafting station.

data.name: Trigger Reset Systems
data.description: Fast-moving threats leave little margin for hesitation. Close encounters with Skulkers could reveal ways to improve paced combat effectiveness.

data.name: Tropical Duck
data.description: It quietly dreams of taking to the skies with its brethren.
data.flavor_text: Can be thrown to create noise
data.article: The Tropical Duck is a trinket, similar to the Rubber Duck. You can throw it to create a noise, which can distract enemies. It can also be kept in your stash to decorate your Raider Den. This item is found inside chimneys when Bird City is active. Other duck variants include the Alien Duck, Doodly Duck, Familiar Duck, Flashy Duck, and Gentle Duck.

data.name: Turbine Compressor
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
The Turbine Compressor is a component used in crafting and specific game projects. It is combined with a Power Rod at a Utility Station to craft a Powered Descender, which is unlocked by the Powered Descender Blueprint. This item is also needed for an Expedition 4 project, alongside other items such as ARC Motion Core, Exodus Modules, and Speaker Component.

You can obtain Turbine Compressors by defeating Turbines. It is also dropped by Courier ARCs. Additionally, the Turbine Compressor can be recycled into salvage.

data.name: Turbo Pump
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Turbo Pump is a rare item that can be recycled to obtain crafting materials.

data.name: "Twilight Compass" Ship Model
data.description: A spirited up-and-comer, this two-master has been known to sail ever so slightly beyond the horizon.
data.article:
The "Twilight Compass" Ship Model is an Uncommon Trinket. You can place this ship model in your Raider Den to decorate it.

You can keep track of items needed for various projects using the Needed Items Tracker.

data.name: Unknown ARC Circuitry
data.description: A bundle of ARC circuitry, unfamiliar in both layout and design.

data.name: Unusable Weapon
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
The Unusable Weapon cannot be equipped or fired. Its main purpose is to be recycled for valuable crafting materials.

It is primarily found inside containers during raids. Most frequently found in the Spaceport map, it can also be found in the Blue Gate, Dam Battlegrounds, and Stella Montis maps. When recycled, it provides coins and other crafting materials.

data.name: Vaporizer Regulator
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
The Vaporizer Regulator is a component used for crafting and completing specific projects. At a Gunsmith crafting station, you can combine it with other items to craft a Dolabra, provided you have the Dolabra Blueprint. It is also needed for Stage 4 of the Expedition 4 project, joining other materials.

You acquire Vaporizer Regulators by defeating Vaporizers and Couriers. This item can also be recycled or salvaged for other materials.

data.name: Vase
data.description: Worth a small fortune.
data.article: The Vase is a rare trinket valued at 3,000 coins. Its main purpose is to be sold to earn coins. You can obtain this item by scavenging in Old World, Residential, and Commercial areas found within the map.

data.name: "Velocity" Ship Model
data.description: Optimized for performance, this marvel of technology sure hopes you weren't planning on packing a particularly elaborate lunch.
data.article:
The "Velocity" Ship Model is a trinket used to decorate your Hideout. You can place it in your stash for display.

Raiders can obtain this item by scavenging in the lower-level utility rooms of the apartments found within the Dam Battlegrounds map.

data.name: Venator Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Venator. Fires two shots at a time.
data.article: The Venator Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Venator at a crafting station.

data.name: Venator I
data.description: Fires two shots at a time.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Venator I is a semi-automatic pistol that fires two shots with each trigger pull, using one unit of medium ammo. This makes it effective for close to medium-range combat.

Raiders can find this item by scavenging or craft it once they have learned the Venator Blueprint, requiring Gunsmith. It can also be recycled or salvaged to obtain other materials.

data.name: Venator II
data.description: Fires two shots at a time.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Venator II is an upgraded version of the Venator I semi-automatic pistol. It fires two shots with each pull of the trigger while only using one unit of medium ammo, making it effective in close to medium-range fights. This specific version offers improved fire rate, faster reloading, and increased durability compared to its base model.

Raiders can obtain the Venator II by crafting it at the Gunsmith using a Venator I along with other crafting materials.

data.name: Venator III
data.description: Fires two shots at a time.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Venator III is an enhanced version of the Venator II pistol, designed for effective close to medium-range combat. It functions as a semi-automatic weapon that uniquely fires two projectiles with each trigger pull, yet only uses one unit of medium ammo per shot.

To obtain this weapon, craft it at a Gunsmith Bench level 1, commonly found in your Hideout. This process requires a Venator II along with other general crafting materials. As an upgrade, it comes with a 26% increased fire rate, 33% reduced reload time, and an additional 20 durability compared to its previous version.

data.name: Venator IV
data.description: Fires two shots at a time.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Venator IV is an advanced version of the Venator semi-automatic pistol, designed for effective close to medium-range combat. It fires two shots with each trigger pull while only consuming one unit of medium ammo. This pistol offers a significantly increased fire rate, a faster reload time, and improved durability compared to the base Venator I.

You obtain the Venator IV by upgrading a Venator III at a Gunsmith bench. The initial Venator I requires a learned Venator Blueprint to craft. It can also be recycled or salvaged to obtain resources.

data.name: Vertical Grip I
data.description: Slightly reduces vertical recoil.
data.article: The Vertical Grip I is a weapon modification used to improve weapon control. Attaching this grip to a compatible weapon helps to reduce the amount of upward movement (vertical recoil) when you fire, making it easier to keep your shots on target.

data.name: Vertical Grip II
data.description: Moderately reduces vertical recoil.
data.article:
The Vertical Grip II is a modification you can attach under your weapon. Its main job is to help you control your weapon better by reducing how much it kicks upwards when you fire.

Craft this item at a Gunsmith station using the Vertical Grip II Blueprint.

data.name: Vertical Grip II Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Vertical Grip II
data.article: The Vertical Grip II Blueprint is a blueprint used at the Gunsmith Bench level 1 that allows you to create the Vertical Grip II, an underbarrel weapon modification. Attaching this modification to a compatible weapon helps reduce its vertical recoil.

data.name: Vertical Grip III
data.description: Significantly reduces vertical recoil.
data.flavor_text: 30% Reduced ADS Speed
data.article:
Vertical Grip III is a weapon modification designed to significantly reduce a weapon's vertical recoil. Applying this grip will also make you aim down sights a little slower.

You can craft this item at the Gunsmith using the Vertical Grip III Blueprint.

data.name: Vertical Grip III Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Vertical Grip III
data.article:
The Vertical Grip III Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Vertical Grip III weapon mod at the Gunsmith. This mod greatly reduces a weapon's vertical recoil by 40%, helping you maintain accuracy during combat.

It can also be recycled for coins.

data.name: Very Comfortable Pillow
data.description: The envy of every Raider. Like sleeping on an especially ergonomic cloud.
data.article:
The Very Comfortable Pillow is a Trinket item.

It is used to improve workshop capabilities, specifically when upgrading the Scrappy workshop.

You can obtain this item by scavenging within Residential and Commercial areas on maps.

data.name: Vintage Steering Wheel
data.description: A harmonious artifact of three-way symmetry, some Nomads believe this to be an ancient reliquary honoring the lunar, the solar and the terrestrial.

data.name: Vita Shot
data.description: A medical item that restores a large amount of health.
data.article:
The Vita Shot is a medical item designed to restore a large amount of a Raider's health after a short delay, helping them recover quickly during engagements. You can sometimes find it while scavenging during your raids.

Alternatively, it can be crafted at Medical Lab once you have learned the Vita Shot Blueprint. If you have extra, it can be recycled into other resources.

data.name: Vita Shot Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Vita Shot - A medical item that restores a large amount of health.
data.article: The Vita Shot Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft vita shots at the Medical Lab. A vita shot is a medical item that restores a large amount of health when used. This blueprint has been observed to be found by Raiders in the Stella Montis map, particularly during medical night raids.

data.name: Vita Spray
data.description: A medical item that continuously restores health during use. Can be used on yourself or your allies.
data.flavor_text: Health Per Second: 10/s
data.article:
The Vita Spray is a medical item that continuously restores health. You can use it on yourself or your allies to regain health over time during raids.

You can find this item by scavenging in the environment. It can also be crafted at a Medical Lab once you have learned the Vita Spray Blueprint. It can be recycled for various resources.

data.name: Vita Spray Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Vita Spray
data.article: The Vita Spray Blueprint is a blueprint used at the Medical Lab to craft Vita Spray. This medical item continuously restores health when used, either on yourself or an ally.

data.name: Volcanic Rock
data.description: Can be thrown.
data.article: Volcanic Rock offers gameplay benefits. Raiders can use this resource to gain advantages during their raids.

data.name: Voltage Converter
data.description: Used in crafting.
data.article:
The Voltage Converter is a material used in crafting. You can use it at a gear bench to create certain gear, and at an explosives station to create certain explosives. It can also be recycled into other useful resources.

You can find this item by scavenging in the environment. It is also available for purchase from Celeste for 10 coins, with a daily limit of 5. Another way to get it is by recycling or salvaging other items.

data.name: Vulcano Blueprint
data.description: Allows you to craft the Vulcano.
data.article: The Vulcano Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft at the Refiner. You can find it by searching various containers during the Hidden Bunker map condition and by searching First Wave Caches during Hurricane map condition. Another rare blueprint you might find is the Tempest Blueprint.

data.name: Vulcano I
data.description: Has good bullet spread but sharp falloff.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Vulcano I is a semi-automatic shotgun that uses shotgun ammo. This weapon is well-suited for close-range combat due to its wide bullet spread, though its effectiveness drops off quickly at longer distances. Raiders craft it at a Gunsmith, provided they have learned the Vulcano Blueprint. It serves as a base for crafting more advanced versions, such as the Vulcano II.

data.name: Vulcano II
data.description: Has good bullet spread but sharp falloff.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Vulcano II is a semi-automatic shotgun, representing an upgraded version of the Vulcano I. This weapon improves upon its predecessor by offering an increased fire rate, reduced reload time, and better durability for enhanced combat performance.

You can obtain this item by crafting it at the Gunsmith, upgrading a Vulcano I using various components. It can also be recycled to gain various resources.

data.name: Vulcano III
data.description: Has good bullet spread but sharp falloff.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Vulcano III is an upgraded semi-automatic shotgun designed for combat encounters. It improves upon earlier versions of the weapon by offering a higher fire rate, quicker reload time, and increased durability. This weapon uses shotgun ammo.

Raiders craft the Vulcano III at a Gunsmith by combining various components.

data.name: Vulcano IV
data.description: Has good bullet spread but sharp falloff.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article:
The Vulcano IV is the final version of the Vulcano semi-automatic shotgun line. It is a weapon designed for combat, utilizing ammunition. This particular version features improved performance attributes such as an increased fire rate, reduced reload time, and enhanced durability.

Raiders can craft the Vulcano IV at Gunsmith. This weapon can also be recycled to gain various resources.

data.name: Warden (Outfit)
data.description: This is the Warden cosmetic outfit
data.article: The Warden (Outfit) is a cosmetic item that changes the visual appearance of your character. It offers different color options to customize your character's look.

data.name: Wasp Driver
data.description: Can be recycled into ARC Alloy.
data.article:
The Wasp Driver is a throwable item that explodes if it is shot after being thrown, dealing damage to nearby ARCs and Raiders.

Raiders obtain this item by defeating Wasps, Wasp Husks, and Couriers.

This item is used in crafting projects and is needed for the The Trifecta quest. Additionally, it can be recycled for resources or salvaged for materials.

data.name: Water Filter
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
The Water Filter is a component that can be recycled into crafting materials, providing basic components for other items.

You can find this item by scavenging inside metal crates, commonly located in industrial areas:

  • Look in the west tunnels of the Research and Administration area, and also within the Power Generation Complex, both in the Dam Battlegrounds map.
  • Search the Shipping Warehouse in the Spaceport map.

data.name: Water Pump
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Water Pump is a rare item that Raiders can recycle for crafting materials and coins. It is also needed for the Unexpected Initiative quest. You can typically find this item inside industrial loot containers like Metal Crates, often located on carts or shelves. Specific areas to check include the Research and Administration west tunnels and Power Generation Complex in the Dam, and the Shipping Warehouse in the Spaceport.

data.name: White Flag
data.description: A deployable white flag.
data.article: The White Flag is a utility item that Raiders can set down or wave during their raids. It is crafted using the White Flag Blueprint at a Medical Lab. Once crafted, it can also be recycled into salvage.

data.name: White Flag Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a White Flag

guide_links.label: How to Find White Flag Blueprint

data.article: The White Flag Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft a white flag.

data.name: White Indigo (Warden Color)
data.description: A new cosmetic variant will be added to your collection
data.article: The White Indigo (Warden Color) is a customization item used to change the appearance of the Warden outfit. Applying this color variant allows you to personalize the look of your character's gear.

data.name: "Wind Sprite" Ship Model
data.description: Undaunted in the face of its larger brethren, this nimble one-master has been known to brave even the most just-above-average of waves.
data.article:
The "Wind Sprite" Ship Model is a common trinket that can be used to decorate your Raider Den. Finding and extracting with this model also provides bonus Merits, which help you progress along the Miniature Voyages reward track during the Last Resort event.

You can obtain the "Wind Sprite" Ship Model by finding it as a loose item on furniture and inside residential containers. It commonly appears in the Hotel area on the Riven Tides map, and can also be found on other maps like the Buried City and Blue Gate.

data.name: Wires
data.description: Used to craft a wide range of items. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
Wires are primarily used to craft various mod components. They are also needed to complete the After Rain Comes and Eyes On The Prize quests, as well as for the Expedition project.

You can find them by searching electrical and technological objects in the environment. They can also be obtained by recycling salvage or purchased from Celeste.

data.name: Wolfpack
data.description: A grenade that scatters into multiple homing missiles, each one targeting ARC and dealing explosive damage on impact.
data.article:
The Wolfpack is an explosive item that, when thrown, scatters into 12 homing missiles. These missiles automatically target nearby ARCs, exploding on impact to deal damage. It is particularly effective for dealing with larger ARCs and is considered a more powerful version of the Seeker Grenade.

Raiders craft this item at an Explosives Station after acquiring the Wolfpack Blueprint.

data.name: Wolfpack Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Wolfpack
data.article:
The Wolfpack Blueprint is a blueprint used at an Explosives Station to craft the Wolfpack grenade.

Once deployed, this grenade scatters into 12 individual homing missiles that quickly seek out and explode on impact with nearby ARCs. It is particularly effective for dealing significant damage to larger ARCs like the Rocketeer, Bastion, Bombardier, and Leaper.

data.name: Yank Grenade
data.description: A grenade that anchors a line to whatever it hits, pulling the target toward the point of impact.

data.name: Yank Grenade Blueprint

data.name: Zipline
data.description: A deployable zipline that allows you to quickly move between two locations.
data.article:
The Zipline is a utility item that helps you travel quickly between two spots. You can attach it to most surfaces to create a fast path between locations, making travel more efficient.

You can craft this item at a Utility Station. It can also be purchased from Apollo for coins, with a daily limit of three. Additionally, you can find ziplines within Raider Deck AR/RD 001 and Raider Deck AR/RD 002. When no longer needed, it can be recycled for basic resources.
